title.en: Volume 40 Biographies 21: Emperor Wu's Seventeen Princes

sentences.zh: 竟陵文宣王子良

translations.literal: Prince Jingling, the Cultured and Propagating, Ziliang
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ziliang, Prince of Jingling, posthumously styled the Cultured and Propagating

sentences.zh: 竟陵文宣王子良字雲英，世祖第二子也。

translations.literal: Prince Jingling, the Cultured and Propagating, Ziliang, styled Yunying, was the second son of the Shizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ziliang, Prince of Jingling styled the Cultured and Propagating, with the courtesy name Yunying, was the second son of Emperor Wu of Qi.

sentences.zh: 初，沈攸之難，隨世祖在盆城，板寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: At first, during Shen Youzhi's rebellion, he followed the Shizu Emperor at Pencheng and was appointed General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, during the uprising of Shen Youzhi, he accompanied the future Emperor Wu at Pencheng and was appointed General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 仍爲宋邵陵王左軍行參軍，轉主簿，安南記室參軍，邵陵王友，王名友，不廢此官。

translations.literal: He then served as Acting Left Army Mobile Aide on the staff of the Prince of Shaoling of Song, was transferred to Chief Clerk, Secretariat Aide of the Pacification Army, and Companion to the Prince of Shaoling; the prince's personal name was You, yet this office was not abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He then served as acting mobile aide on the left army staff of Liu You, Prince of Shaoling of Song, became chief clerk, then secretariat aide of the Pacification Army and companion to the prince; although the prince's personal name was You, the title Companion to the Prince of Shaoling was retained.

sentences.zh: 遷安南長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Senior Administrator of the Pacification Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to senior administrator on the Pacification Army staff.

sentences.zh: ，爲使持節、都督會稽東陽臨海永嘉新安五郡、輔國將軍、會稽太守。

translations.literal: [He] was made Bearer of the Staff with full discretionary powers, Area Commander of the five commanderies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, and Xin'an, General Who Supports the State, and Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed bearer of the staff with full discretionary powers, area commander of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, and Xin'an, General Who Supports the State, and administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 宋世元嘉中，皆責成郡縣；

translations.literal: During the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty, all levies were imposed directly on the commanderies and counties;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song, in the Yuanjia period, the court held commanderies and counties directly responsible for collections;

sentences.zh: 孝武徵求急速，以郡縣遲緩，始遣臺使，自此公役勞擾。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu demanded payment with urgency; because the commanderies and counties were slow, court envoys were first dispatched, and from this time public service and corvée became a constant burden.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu pressed collections with such haste that, when local governments lagged, the court began sending its own envoys; from then on public labor and levies became ceaselessly oppressive.

sentences.zh: 太祖踐阼，子良陳之曰：

translations.literal: When the founding emperor ascended the throne, Ziliang submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao took the throne, Ziliang memorialized the throne as follows:

sentences.zh: :　　前臺使督逋切調，恒聞相望於道。

translations.literal: Formerly, court envoys pressing for arrears and urgent collections could constantly be heard passing one another on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Before I took office, envoys from the capital driving collections of arrears and urgent levies were always to be seen meeting one another on the highways.

sentences.zh: 及臣至郡，亦殊不疏。

translations.literal: When I reached my commandery, the situation was by no means uncommon.
translations.idiomatic: By the time I reached my prefecture, the same abuses were anything but rare.

sentences.zh: 凡此輩使人，旣非詳慎懃順，或貪險崎嶇，要求此役。

translations.literal: All such envoys are neither careful nor dutiful and compliant; some are greedy and treacherous, demanding this assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Such agents are seldom conscientious or obedient; many are grasping and ruthless, and they actively seek these missions.

sentences.zh: 朝辭禁門，情態卽異；

translations.literal: When they take leave of the Forbidden Gate in the morning, their manner is already altered;
translations.idiomatic: They leave the palace gates in the morning with one demeanor;

sentences.zh: 暮宿村縣，威福便行。

translations.literal: by evening, lodging in villages and counties, they wield authority and favor at will.
translations.idiomatic: by nightfall, encamped in town or village, they exercise arbitrary power as they please.

sentences.zh: 但令朱鼓裁完，鈹槊微具，顧眄左右，叱吒自專。

translations.literal: Once the red drums are barely assembled and spears and halberds slightly provided, they glance about and shout orders on their own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Give them only a painted drum half rigged and a few spears and halberds, and they already glare about and bark commands like lords of all they survey.

sentences.zh: 擿宗斷族，排輕斥重，脅遏津埭，恐喝傳郵。

translations.literal: They pick out clans and cut off lineages, push aside the weak and reject the powerful, coerce ferry crossings and embankments, and intimidate relay stations.
translations.idiomatic: They single out whole lineages for ruin, bully the humble and snub the eminent, extort at every ferry and dam, and terrorize the postal relays.

sentences.zh: 破崗水逆，商旅半引，逼令到下，先過己船。

translations.literal: At Pogang, against the current, merchants' boats are half towed; they force them downstream, but their own boats pass first.
translations.idiomatic: At Pogang, where the current runs contrary, they make merchant vessels tow half their length, then force them downstream—yet their own boats always pass ahead.

sentences.zh: 浙江風猛，公私畏渡，脫舫在前，驅令俱發。

translations.literal: On the Zhe River the winds are fierce and both public and private parties fear crossing; they detach a boat ahead and drive all to set out together.
translations.idiomatic: On the Zhe River, where gales are fierce and everyone dreads the crossing, they launch a light craft first and then drive every other boat to follow at once.

sentences.zh: 呵蹙行民，固其常理。

translations.literal: Shouting at and driving traveling commoners is for them an ordinary practice.
translations.idiomatic: Bawling at wayfarers and hustling the people along is, for them, merely routine.

sentences.zh: 侮折守宰，出變無窮。

translations.literal: They insult and humiliate prefects and magistrates, producing endless variations of abuse.
translations.idiomatic: They humiliate local administrators, inventing fresh outrages without end.

sentences.zh: 旣瞻郭望境，便飛下嚴符，但稱行臺，未顯所督。

translations.literal: Once they sight the outer wall and view the border of a district, they immediately dispatch stern orders, calling themselves only the Mobile Office without revealing whom they supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly have they glimpsed a city's walls when they fling down harsh writs, styling themselves the itinerant bureau while never stating whose authority they represent.

sentences.zh: 先訶彊寺，却攝羣曹，開亭正，便振荊革。

translations.literal: First they rebuke the powerful, then they seize control of all offices; once court is opened, they at once wield the whip.
translations.idiomatic: First they browbeat the powerful, then they take charge of every office; open a hearing, and they are already flourishing the rod.

sentences.zh: 其次絳標寸紙，一日數至；

translations.literal: Next come red labels on slips of paper, arriving several times in a single day;
translations.idiomatic: Next come crimson notices on scraps of paper, several in a single day;

sentences.zh: 徵村切里，俄刻十催。

translations.literal: summoning villages and pressing hamlets, within moments issuing ten rounds of urgent demand.
translations.idiomatic: summoning whole villages and pressing every hamlet, issuing ten rounds of dunning within the hour.

sentences.zh: 四鄉所召，莫辨枉直，孩老士庶，具令付獄。

translations.literal: Those summoned from the four directions cannot tell right from wrong; infants, the aged, gentry, and commoners are all ordered cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Those summoned from every quarter cannot tell justice from abuse; children, the elderly, scholars, and commoners alike are thrown into jail.

sentences.zh: 或尺布之逋，曲以當匹；

translations.literal: sometimes an arrears of a foot of cloth is twisted to count as a whole bolt;
translations.idiomatic: a debt of a few feet of cloth may be reckoned as a full bolt;

sentences.zh: 百錢餘稅，且增爲千。

translations.literal: a surplus tax of a hundred cash is then raised to a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: a tax shortfall of a hundred cash is inflated to a thousand.

sentences.zh: 或誑應質作尚方，寄繫東冶，萬姓駭迫，人不自固。

translations.literal: Some are deceived into answering that they are pledged to the Imperial Workshop and are detained at the Eastern Smeltery; the myriad people are terrified and pressed, and no one feels secure.
translations.idiomatic: Some are tricked into confessing pawn service at the Imperial Workshop and are held at the Eastern Prison; the people are terrorized, and no one dares feel safe.

sentences.zh: 遂漂衣敗力，競致兼漿。

translations.literal: Thus they pawn clothing and exhaust their strength, competing to bring double portions of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Families pawn their clothes and ruin their strength, vying to supply feasts of meat and wine.

sentences.zh: 值今夕酒諧肉飫，卽許附申赦格；

translations.literal: If tonight's wine is harmonious and the meat abundant, they at once permit a petition under the amnesty statute;
translations.idiomatic: if tonight's feast is ample with wine and meat, they promise to file for amnesty;

sentences.zh: 明日禮輕貨薄，便復不入恩科。

translations.literal: if tomorrow the gifts are light and goods meager, the case again falls outside the grace rolls.
translations.idiomatic: if tomorrow's gifts are slight, the case again falls outside mercy.

sentences.zh: 筐貢微闕，緫撻肆情，風塵毀謗，隨忿而發。

translations.literal: If basket-tribute is slightly deficient, they flog at will; slander born of resentment is vented as anger moves them.
translations.idiomatic: A trifling shortfall in basket-tribute brings a beating at whim; calumnies fly wherever their temper turns.

sentences.zh: 及其蒜轉積，鵝栗漸盈，遠則分鬻他境，近則託貿吏民。

translations.literal: When their stores of garlic and piles of grain and geese and chestnuts gradually fill, far off they divide and sell in other regions, near at hand they entrust trade to clerks and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: When their hoards of garlic, grain, geese, and chestnuts mount, they peddle the surplus in distant markets or pass it through local clerks and townspeople.

sentences.zh: 反請郡邑，助民申緩，回刺言臺，推信在所。

translations.literal: They then ask the commandery and county to help the people petition for relief, while secretly reporting to the court and shifting trust to their own locale.
translations.idiomatic: They urge the prefecture to plead for the people while secretly denouncing the capital and claiming credit locally.

sentences.zh: 如聞頃者令長守牧，離此每實，非復近歲。

translations.literal: I have heard that recently magistrates and regional governors have kept their distance from such practices in fact, unlike in recent years.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that magistrates and governors have lately, in truth, kept their distance from such abuses—unlike in recent years.

sentences.zh: 愚謂凡諸檢課，宜停遣使，密畿州郡，則指賜勑令，遙外鎮宰，明下條源，旣各奉別旨，人競自罄。

translations.literal: I humbly hold that for all inspections and collections, dispatch of envoys should cease; for commanderies near the capital, imperial edicts should be sent directly; for distant frontier governors, regulations should be clearly promulgated—once each holds separate instructions, men will compete to exhaust themselves in service.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that inspections and collections should no longer rely on dispatched envoys: near the capital, issue edicts directly; in distant provinces, publish clear rules—once each officer holds his own charge, men will strive of themselves to fulfill it.

sentences.zh: 雖復臺使盈湊，會取正屬所辦，徒相疑僨，反更淹懈。

translations.literal: Even if court envoys crowd in numbers, matters still fall to the proper officials to handle; they merely suspect and frustrate one another, and work grows more slack and delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Even when envoys swarm, the work still belongs to the regular officials; they only breed mutual suspicion and delay.

sentences.zh: :　　凡預衣冠，荷恩盛世，多以闇緩貽諐，少爲欺猾入罪。

translations.literal: All who wear caps and robes and have received favor in this flourishing age mostly err through dullness and laxity, and few are convicted for fraud and sharp practice.
translations.idiomatic: Those of the gentry who have enjoyed favor in this age mostly offend through negligence rather than fraud.

sentences.zh: 若類以宰牧乖政，則觸事難委，不容課逋上綱，偏覺非才。

translations.literal: If one classifies them with governors who misgovern, then on every matter trust is hard to place; they cannot be allowed to report arrears upward, and one feels they are simply not capable.
translations.idiomatic: If we treat them like incompetent governors, nothing can be entrusted to them and arrears cannot be reported upward without seeming unjust.

sentences.zh: 但賒促差降，各限一期。

translations.literal: Only grant extensions with graded reductions, each limited to one term.
translations.idiomatic: Grant graded extensions, each for a fixed term.

sentences.zh: 如乃事速應緩，自依違糾坐之。

translations.literal: If affairs that should be slow are rushed, or those that should be urgent are delayed, let penalties for disobedience be applied accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: If urgency and delay are reversed, let the usual penalties for dereliction apply.

sentences.zh: 坐之之科，不必須重，但令必行，期在可肅。

translations.literal: The statutes of punishment need not be severe, but orders must be enforced, with the aim that discipline may be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Penalties need not be harsh, provided they are enforced, so that order may be restored.

sentences.zh: 且兩裝之船，充擬千緒；

translations.literal: Moreover, boats with double outfitting are reckoned at a thousand items;
translations.idiomatic: A single mission may require a thousand items aboard two fully laden boats;

sentences.zh: 三坊寡役，呼訂萬計。

translations.literal: the three workshops' sparse labor is summoned to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: and corvée from the three workshops is requisitioned by the ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 每一事之發，彌晨方辦，粗計近遠，率遣一部，職散人領，無減二十，舟船所資，皆復稱是。

translations.literal: Each time an affair arises, it takes from dawn till full day to prepare; roughly calculating near and far, generally a whole section is sent, offices scattered and men leading, never fewer than twenty; what boats and ships require is again declared adequate.
translations.idiomatic: Each undertaking takes from dawn to dusk to prepare; near or far, a whole section is sent, never fewer than twenty men, and every item for the voyage is again declared indispensable.

sentences.zh: 長江萬里，費固倍之。

translations.literal: The Yangzi stretches ten thousand li, and costs naturally double.
translations.idiomatic: Along the ten thousand li of the Yangzi, costs naturally multiply.

sentences.zh: 較略一年，脫得省者，息船優役，寔爲不少。

translations.literal: Comparing roughly over one year, if savings could be achieved, reducing boats and easing corvée would truly be considerable.
translations.idiomatic: A year's reckoning shows that ending such missions would spare vast expense in shipping and labor.

sentences.zh: 兼折姦減竊，遠近蹔安。

translations.literal: At the same time, curbing wickedness and reducing theft, near and far would for a time be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Fraud and petty theft would decline as well, and the realm would know a measure of peace.

sentences.zh: 封聞喜縣公，邑千五百戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Wenxi County with a fief of one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Wenxi with a fief of fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 子良敦義愛古。

translations.literal: Ziliang was sincere in righteousness and loved antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang was earnest in duty and devoted to antiquity.

sentences.zh: 郡民朱百年有至行，先卒，賜其妻米百斛，蠲一民給其薪蘇。

translations.literal: A man of the commandery, Zhu Bainian, possessed supreme conduct but had died earlier; [Ziliang] granted his wife a hundred hu of grain and exempted one commoner to supply her fuel.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Bainian, a commandery man of exemplary conduct, died, Ziliang granted his widow a hundred hu of grain and excused one household from service to provide her firewood.

sentences.zh: 郡閤下有虞翻舊牀，罷任還，乃致以歸。

translations.literal: In the commandery hall there was an old couch of Yu Fan; when he left office and returned, he had it sent back to its owner.
translations.idiomatic: In the prefectural hall stood an old couch once used by Yu Fan; when Ziliang left office, he had it returned to Yu's family.

sentences.zh: 後於西邸起古齋，多聚古人器服以充之。

translations.literal: Later, at his western residence he built an antiquarian studio and gathered many ancient vessels and garments to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: Later he built an antiquarian hall in his western mansion and filled it with ancient vessels and costume.

sentences.zh: 夏禹廟盛有禱祀，子良曰：「禹泣辜表仁，菲食旌約，服翫果粽，足以致誠。

translations.literal: The temple of Yu of Xia had lavish prayer offerings; Ziliang said: "Yu wept over the guilty to display benevolence and ate sparingly to signal restraint; fruit and rice dumplings as offerings suffice to show sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: The Temple of Yu of Xia was given to lavish rites; Ziliang said, "Yu wept over the guilty to show benevolence and ate frugally to teach restraint—fruit and rice dumplings are enough to express sincerity."

sentences.zh: 」使歲獻扇簟而已。

translations.literal: " He had only fans and mats presented each year.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered only fans and mats presented each year.

sentences.zh: 建元二年，穆妃薨，去官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, Consort Mu died, and he left office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyuan (480), when Consort Mu died, he resigned his post.

sentences.zh: 仍爲征虜將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: He was then made General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed General Who Punishes the Barbarians and intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 開私倉賑屬縣貧民。

translations.literal: He opened his private granaries to relieve the poor of subordinate counties.
translations.idiomatic: He opened his private granaries to relieve the poor in the counties under his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 明年，上表曰：「京尹雖居都邑，而境壤兼跨，廣袤周輪，幾將千里。

translations.literal: The next year he submitted a memorial, saying: "Although the Intendant of the Capital resides in the metropolitan region, his territory also spans other districts; in breadth and circumference it approaches a thousand li."
translations.idiomatic: The following year he memorialized: "Though the capital intendant sits in the metropolis, his jurisdiction is vast—nearly a thousand li in circuit."

sentences.zh: 縈原抱隰，其處甚多，舊遏古塘，非唯一所。

translations.literal: There are many places where plains encircle marshes; old embankments and ancient ponds are not in one place alone.
translations.idiomatic: Lowlands ring many upland basins, and old dikes and ponds are scattered everywhere.

sentences.zh: 而民貧業廢，地利久蕪。

translations.literal: Yet the people are poor and their occupations abandoned; the land's advantage has long lain fallow.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people are poor, fields lie abandoned, and the land's productivity has long been wasted.

sentences.zh: 近啓遣五官殷濔、典籤劉僧瑗到諸縣循履，得丹陽、溧陽、永世等四縣解，并村耆辭列，堪墾之田，合計荒熟有八千五百五十四頃，脩治塘遏，可用十一萬八千餘夫，一春就功，便可成立。

translations.literal: Recently I sent the Five Offices officer Yin Mi and Secretariat Aide Liu Sengyuan to tour the counties; from Danyang, Liyang, Yongshi, and four other counties I received reports, together with village elders' statements listing fields fit for reclamation—altogether wasteland and mature land totaling eight thousand five hundred fifty-four qing; repairing ponds and embankments would require more than one hundred eighteen thousand laborers, and in one spring the work could be completed.
translations.idiomatic: I recently sent Yin Mi of the Five Offices and Liu Sengyuan, secretariat aide, to survey the counties. Reports from Danyang, Liyang, Yongshi, and three other counties, with statements from village elders, show eight thousand five hundred fifty-four qing ready for cultivation; repairing dikes and ponds would take some one hundred eighteen thousand laborers, work that could be finished in a single spring.

sentences.zh: 」上納之。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 會遷官，事寢。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to another office, the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred, the project lapsed.

sentences.zh: 是年，始制東宮官僚以下官敬子良。

translations.literal: That year, regulations were first made for Eastern Palace officials and those below to show respect to Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: That year it was first decreed that Eastern Palace officials and all lower ranks should show deference to Ziliang.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，封竟陵郡王，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor took the throne, [Ziliang] was enfeoffed as Prince of Jingling Commandery with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Ziliang was enfeoffed as Prince of Jingling with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 爲使持節、都督南徐兖二州諸軍事、鎮北將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was made Bearer of the Staff with full discretionary powers, Area Commander of the military affairs of the two provinces of Southern Xuzhou and Yanzhou, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed bearer of the staff, area commander of Southern Xuzhou and Yanzhou, General Who Pacifies the North, and inspector of Southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，徙爲侍中、都督南兖兖徐青冀五州、征北將軍、南兖州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming, he was transferred to Attendant at Court, Area Commander of the five provinces of Southern Yanzhou, Yanzhou, Xuzhou, Qingzhou, and Jizhou, General Who Campaigns North, and Inspector of Southern Yanzhou, holding the staff as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongming (483), he became attendant at court, area commander of Southern Yanzhou, Yanzhou, Xuzhou, Qingzhou, and Jizhou, General Who Campaigns North, and inspector of Southern Yanzhou, retaining his staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 給油絡車。

translations.literal: He was granted an oil-varnished carriage with a canopy net.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a lacquered carriage with a canopy net.

sentences.zh: 明年，入爲護軍將軍，兼司徒，領兵置佐，侍中如故。

translations.literal: The next year he entered [the capital] as General Who Protects the Army, concurrently Minister of Education, with troops and staff appointed, Attendant at Court as before.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he entered the capital as General Who Protects the Army and concurrent minister of education, with military staff appointed, while retaining his post as attendant.

sentences.zh: 鎮西州。

translations.literal: He garrisoned the Western Province.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned the Western Province quarter of the capital.

sentences.zh: 三年，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was granted one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was granted a full set of martial music.

sentences.zh: 四年，進號車騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, his title was advanced to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 子良少有清尚，禮才好士，居不疑之地，傾意賔客，天下才學皆遊集焉。

translations.literal: Ziliang from youth had pure and lofty tastes, loved ritual and music and honored scholars; occupying a position free from suspicion, he poured his heart into guests, and men of talent and learning throughout the realm all gathered there.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Ziliang cultivated refined tastes, loved ceremony and learning, and honored scholars; secure in his position as the emperor's brother, he lavished attention on guests until men of talent from across the realm flocked to his house.

sentences.zh: 善立勝事，夏月客至，爲設瓜飲及甘果，著之文教。

translations.literal: He was skilled at creating elegant occasions; when guests came in summer, he set out melon drinks and sweet fruits, recording them in literary instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in elegant entertainments; when guests came in summer he served melon drinks and fruit, customs he recorded in his literary salon.

sentences.zh: 士子文章及朝貴辭翰，皆發教撰錄。

translations.literal: Essays by scholars and writings by court nobles were all issued under his patronage for compilation and recording.
translations.idiomatic: Essays by scholars and writings by courtiers were all commissioned and collected under his patronage.

sentences.zh: 是時上新親政，水旱不時。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had newly taken personal rule, and flood and drought came out of season.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had lately assumed personal rule, and floods and droughts struck out of season.

sentences.zh: 子良密啓曰：

translations.literal: Ziliang submitted a secret memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang submitted a confidential memorial:

sentences.zh: :　　臣思水潦成患，良田沃壤，變爲汙澤；

translations.literal: I reflect that flooding has become a calamity and fertile fields of rich soil have turned into mire;
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that floods have become a calamity, turning fertile fields into marshes;

sentences.zh: 農政告祥，因高肆務，播植旣周，繼以旱虐。

translations.literal: the agricultural season reported auspicious signs, work was carried out on the high ground, sowing and planting were completed, and then drought ravaged the land.
translations.idiomatic: the season began auspiciously, planting on the uplands was finished, and then drought struck.

sentences.zh: 黔庶呼嗟，相視褫氣。

translations.literal: The common people cry out in lament, looking at one another with spirits undone.
translations.idiomatic: the people cry out in despair, their spirits broken.

sentences.zh: 夫國資於民，民資於食，匪食匪民，何以能政？

translations.literal: The state relies on the people, the people rely on food—without food there are no people; without people, how can there be government?
translations.idiomatic: The state rests on the people, the people on grain—without grain there are no people, and without people, how can there be government?

sentences.zh: 臣每一念此，寢不便席。

translations.literal: Each time I think of this, I cannot rest easy on my mat.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I think of this, I cannot sleep at ease.

sentences.zh: 本始中，郡國大旱，宣帝下詔除民租。

translations.literal: In the Benshi era, when commanderies and kingdoms suffered great drought, Emperor Xuan issued an edict remitting the people's land tax.
translations.idiomatic: In the Benshi era of Han, when drought struck the realm, Emperor Xuan remitted the land tax.

sentences.zh: 今聞所在逋餘尚多，守宰嚴期，兼夜課切，新稅力尚無從，故調於何取給？

translations.literal: Now I hear that arrears everywhere are still numerous; governors and magistrates enforce strict deadlines and press collections through the night; strength for new taxes is not yet available—from what will old levies be supplied?
translations.idiomatic: I hear arrears remain heavy everywhere, magistrates pressing collections day and night while new taxes cannot be met—whence will old levies be paid?

sentences.zh: 政當相驅爲盜耳。

translations.literal: They will surely drive one another to become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The people will be driven to banditry.

sentences.zh: 愚謂逋租宜皆原除，少降停恩，微紓民命。

translations.literal: I humbly hold that arrears in rent should all be remitted, with a slight lowering and suspension of favor, slightly easing the people's lives.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that all rent arrears should be forgiven, with a modest suspension of collections to ease the people's plight.

sentences.zh: :　　自宋道無章，王風陵替，竊官假號，駢門連室。

translations.literal: Since the Song age governance lacked standards and royal conduct declined, men usurped offices and borrowed titles, filling gates and linking households.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Song, government has lacked order and courtly standards have decayed; men usurp offices and borrow titles until fraudulent households fill every lane.

sentences.zh: 今左民所檢，動以萬數，漸漬之來，非復始適，一朝洗正，理致沸騰。

translations.literal: Now those inspected by the Ministry of the Left Household number tens of thousands; what has seeped in over time is no longer recent—if corrected in a single day, reason itself would boil over.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of the Left Household now investigates cases by the tens of thousands; abuses have accumulated over years, and a single day's purge would throw the realm into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 小人之心，罔思前咎，董之以威，反怨後罰，獸窮則觸，事在匪輕。

translations.literal: The hearts of petty men do not reflect on past fault; drive them with awe and they resent later punishment—when beasts are cornered they strike; the matter is by no means light.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men forget past offenses; threaten them and they resent future punishment—a cornered beast will strike, and the danger is grave.

sentences.zh: 齊有天下日淺，恩洽未布，一方或飢，當加優養。

translations.literal: Qi has held the realm but a short time; favor has not yet spread everywhere; if one region suffers hunger, it should receive added care.
translations.idiomatic: Qi has ruled but briefly; imperial grace has not yet reached every corner; where hunger appears, mercy should be shown.

sentences.zh: 愚謂自可依源削除，未宜便充猥役。

translations.literal: I humbly hold that they should be struck from the registers according to origin, and should not at once be assigned to menial corvée.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that false entries should be struck from the registers by origin, not immediately conscripted for base labor.

sentences.zh: 且部曹檢校，誠存精密，令史奸黠，鮮不容情。

translations.literal: Moreover, though the ministry offices' inspections are truly meticulous, clerks are crafty and seldom spare anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Though ministry inspections are meticulous, clerks are cunning and rarely show mercy.

sentences.zh: 情旣有私，理或枉謬。

translations.literal: When feeling already holds private interest, principle may be bent into error.
translations.idiomatic: Where private interest intrudes, justice may be perverted.

sentences.zh: 耳目有限，羣狡無極。

translations.literal: Eyes and ears are limited, while the crafty are without end.
translations.idiomatic: Officials cannot see everything, while deceit knows no limit.

sentences.zh: 變易是非，居然可見。

translations.literal: Right and wrong are reversed—this is plainly visible.
translations.idiomatic: Right and wrong are reversed before one's eyes.

sentences.zh: 詳而後取，於事未遲。

translations.literal: To examine thoroughly before acting would not be late for the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Thorough inquiry before action would not be too late.

sentences.zh: :　　明詔深矜獄圄，恩文累墜。

translations.literal: Bright edicts deeply pity the prisons, and gracious documents have repeatedly been issued.
translations.idiomatic: Your enlightened edicts have shown deep mercy toward prisoners, and gracious decrees have repeatedly been issued.

sentences.zh: 今科網嚴重，稱爲峻察。

translations.literal: Now the statutes and nets are severe, styled rigorous scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the law has grown severe and is praised as rigorous scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 負罪離諐，充積牢戶。

translations.literal: Those bearing guilt and estranged from propriety fill the prison cells.
translations.idiomatic: The guilty and the errant crowd the prisons.

sentences.zh: 暑時鬱蒸，加以金鐵。

translations.literal: In summer's sweltering heat, with iron fetters added on top.
translations.idiomatic: In summer's oppressive heat, prisoners also wear iron shackles.

sentences.zh: 聚憂之氣，足感天和。

translations.literal: The accumulated qi of grief is enough to move heaven's harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Such accumulated sorrow can disturb heaven's harmony.

sentences.zh: 民之多怨，非國福矣。

translations.literal: The people's great resentment is no blessing to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Widespread popular resentment bodes ill for the realm.

sentences.zh: :　　頃土木之務，甚爲殷廣，雖役未及民，勤費已積。

translations.literal: Recently construction works have been very extensive; though corvée has not yet reached the people, accumulated forced expenditure already piles up.
translations.idiomatic: Recently construction has grown lavish; though corvée has not yet fallen on the people, the cost in labor and funds already mounts.

sentences.zh: 炎旱致災，或由於此。

translations.literal: Scorching drought brings calamity—perhaps for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: The drought and disaster may stem from this.

sentences.zh: 皇明載遠，書軌未一，緣淮帶江，數州地耳，以魏方漢，猶一郡之譬，以今比古，復爲遠矣。

translations.literal: Your sage brilliance extends far, yet written culture and carriage tracks are not united; along the Huai and girding the Yangtze are but a few provinces' territory; measured against Han, Wei is still but one commandery's comparison; compared ancient to modern, it is again remote.
translations.idiomatic: Your radiance reaches far, yet the realm is not united; lands along the Huai and Yangtze are but a few provinces—in size, Qi beside Han is like one commandery beside a great empire, and the present beside antiquity is even more modest.

sentences.zh: 何得不愛其民，緩其政，救其危，存其命哉？

translations.literal: How can one not love the people, ease government, save their peril, and preserve their lives?
translations.idiomatic: How can you not love the people, ease policy, rescue their peril, and preserve their lives?

sentences.zh: :　　湘區奧密，蠻寇熾彊，如聞南師未能挫戮。

translations.literal: The Xiang region is deep and hidden; barbarian bandits burn fierce and strong; I hear the southern army has been unable to break and destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiang region is rugged and remote; barbarian raiders are fierce; I hear the southern forces have not yet crushed them.

sentences.zh: 百姓齊民，積年塗炭，疽食侵淫，邊虞方重。

translations.literal: Common people, the equal masses, for accumulated years in charcoal and ash; ulcer-like eating creeps and spreads; frontier alarms are just now heavy.
translations.idiomatic: The common people have for years been ground down; ruin spreads like a festering sore, and frontier danger grows acute.

sentences.zh: 交州敻絕一垂，寔惟荒服，恃遠後賔，固亦恒事。

translations.literal: Jiaozhou is remote at the furthest verge, truly a wild domain; relying on distance to come late as guest is also a constant affair.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhou lies at the empire's farthest edge, a true frontier land; tardy submission because of distance is nothing new.

sentences.zh: 自青德啓運，款關受職，置之度外，不足絓言。

translations.literal: Since the blue virtue opened the fortune, they knocked at the passes and received office; put outside concern, not worth entangling words.
translations.idiomatic: Since your virtuous reign began they have presented themselves at the passes and accepted office; set beyond urgent concern, they are scarcely worth lengthy discussion.

sentences.zh: 今縣軍遠伐，經途萬里，衆寡事殊，客主勢異，以逸待勞，全勝難必。

translations.literal: Now to suspend the army on a distant campaign, the route ten thousand li, many and few in different circumstances, guest and host in different momentum, with ease awaiting exhaustion—complete victory is hard to assure.
translations.idiomatic: Now to launch a distant expedition, the march ten thousand li, odds unequal and host and guest reversed—awaiting a weary foe from ease, total victory is far from assured.

sentences.zh: 又緣道調兵，以足軍力，民丁烏合，事乖習銳。

translations.literal: Moreover, levying troops along the route to fill military strength—civilian levies flock like crows, affairs contrary to drilled sharpness.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, troops levied along the march to fill the ranks are a rabble of pressed civilians, ill suited to seasoned fighting.

sentences.zh: 廣州積歲無年，越州兵糧素乏，加以發借，必致恇擾。

translations.literal: Guangzhou for accumulated years without harvest, Yuezhou military grain always scarce; adding requisition and borrowing will surely lead to panic and disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou has gone years without a good harvest, and Yuezhou has always lacked military grain; added levies and forced loans will surely breed panic and unrest.

sentences.zh: 愚謂叔獻所請，不宜聽從；

translations.literal: I humbly hold that Shuxian's request should not be heeded;
translations.idiomatic: I submit that Shuxian's request should not be granted;

sentences.zh: 取亂侮亡，更俟後會。

translations.literal: Take disorder and insult the perishing; again await a later occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Seize the enemy when he is in disorder and treat the doomed with contempt—but wait for a more favorable occasion.

sentences.zh: 雖緩歲月，必有可禽之理，差息發動費役之勞。

translations.literal: Though slowing months and years, there must be reason for capture, somewhat easing mobilization and corvée toil.
translations.idiomatic: Though time may pass, they can surely be taken in due course, while easing somewhat the labor of mobilization and corvée.

sentences.zh: 劉楷見甲以助湘中，威力旣舉，蟻寇自服。

translations.literal: Liu Kai, showing armor to aid Xiangzhong—once martial might is raised, ant-like bandits will submit of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Let Liu Kai display armed force to aid the Xiang region; once might is shown, petty raiders will submit of themselves.

sentences.zh: 詔折租布，二分取錢。

translations.literal: An edict discounted rent-cloth, taking money at two-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed rent-cloth to be commuted, collecting cash at twenty percent.

sentences.zh: 子良又啓曰：

translations.literal: Ziliang again memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang again memorialized the throne as follows:

sentences.zh: :　　臣一月入朝，六登玫陛，廣殿稠人，裁奉顏色，縱有所懷，豈敢自達。

translations.literal: In one month attending court, six times ascending the red terrace; in broad halls and dense crowds, barely offering my complexion—even if I have thoughts, how dare I express myself.
translations.idiomatic: In one month at court I have six times ascended the red steps; in vast halls and dense crowds I barely present my face—even when I have concerns, how dare I speak freely.

sentences.zh: 比天眚亟見，地孽亟臻，民下妖訛，好生噂。

translations.literal: Recently heaven's calamities appear repeatedly, earth's portents arrive repeatedly; among the people strange talk, liking to produce slander.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warnings appear again and again, and earthly portents follow; among the people rumors flourish and slander spreads.

sentences.zh: 穀價雖和，比室飢嗛；

translations.literal: Though grain prices are moderate, household after household goes hungry;
translations.idiomatic: Grain may be cheap, yet in home after home there is hunger;

sentences.zh: 縑纊雖賤，駢門躶質。

translations.literal: Though silk is cheap, gates are lined with those stripped and pledged.
translations.idiomatic: Though silk is cheap, every lane has families stripped bare and in pawn.

sentences.zh: 臣一念此，每入心骨。

translations.literal: Each time I think of this, it pierces to the marrow of my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I think of this, it pierces me to the bone.

sentences.zh: 三吳奧區，地惟河、輔，百度所資，罕不自出，宜在蠲優，使其全富。

translations.literal: The Three Wu is a vital region, land like the Yellow River and capital districts; myriad enterprises rely on it, few things not produced there—it ought to receive exemption and favor so that it may be wholly prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Wu is a vital region, the land like the heartland of old; countless needs are supplied from it, and little is not produced there—it should enjoy relief and favor until it is fully prosperous.

sentences.zh: 而守宰相繼，務在裒剋，圍桑品屋，以准貲課。

translations.literal: Yet district chiefs and counsels succeed one another, bent on extraction; they survey mulberry trees and rank houses to set property levies.
translations.idiomatic: Yet magistrates and prefects succeed one another, bent on squeezing the people; they inventory mulberry trees and grade dwellings to set property taxes.

sentences.zh: 致令斬樹發瓦，以充重賦，破民財產，要利一時。

translations.literal: This has led to felling trees and ripping tiles to meet heavy levies, ruining the people's property for a moment's profit.
translations.idiomatic: They have felled trees and torn off roof tiles to meet crushing taxes, destroying people's livelihoods for a moment's gain.

sentences.zh: 東郡使民，年無常限，在所相承，准令上直。

translations.literal: In the eastern commandery, corvée for the people has no fixed annual limit; what each post inherits, they treat as the standard for direct labor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eastern commanderies, corvée has no fixed annual limit; each office simply inherits the prior quota as the standard for labor.

sentences.zh: 每至州臺使命，切求懸急，應充猥役，必由窮困。

translations.literal: Whenever prefectural and ministerial missions come, they press with urgent demands; to meet base corvée, one must come from utter destitution.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever provincial and capital missions arrive, they press with urgent demands; to meet petty corvée assignments, the poorest must bear the burden.

sentences.zh: 乃有畏失嚴期，自殘軀命，亦有斬絕手足，以避傜役。

translations.literal: Some, fearing to miss strict deadlines, mutilate their own lives; some cut off hands or feet to avoid corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Some, fearing to miss harsh deadlines, take their own lives; others cut off hands or feet to escape corvée.

sentences.zh: 生育弗起，殆爲恒事。

translations.literal: Failure to raise children has nearly become routine.
translations.idiomatic: Parents who will not rear children has nearly become routine.

sentences.zh: 守長不務先富民，而唯言益國，豈有民貧於下，而國富於上邪？

translations.literal: Magistrates do not strive first to enrich the people but only speak of enriching the state—can the people be poor below while the state is rich above?
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates do not strive first to enrich the people but only to swell the treasury—can the people be poor below while the state is rich above?

sentences.zh: :　　又泉鑄歲遠，類多翦鑿，江東大錢，十不一在。

translations.literal: Moreover, coinage over many years has largely been clipped and chiseled; of the great coins of the Jiangdong, not one in ten remains.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, coinage has long been clipped and shaved; of the large coins of the lower Yangtze, scarcely one in ten remains intact.

sentences.zh: 公家所受，必須輪郭完全，遂買本一千，加子七百，猶求請無地，棰革相繼。

translations.literal: What the government accepts must have rims wholly complete; thus one buys the original for a thousand and adds seven hundred more, yet still finds no place to plead—beatings and floggings follow in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The government will accept only coins with rims intact; one must buy a thousand-cash coin and pay seven hundred more on top, yet still find no relief—beatings and floggings follow one after another.

sentences.zh: 尋完者爲用，旣不兼兩，回復遷貿，會非委積，徒令小民每嬰困苦。

translations.literal: Seeking only whole coins for use, since they do not suffice for two payments, one returns to trade and exchange; it is not a matter of stored surplus, yet petty folk suffer hardship at every turn.
translations.idiomatic: Because only whole coins are accepted and they cannot serve for two payments, people must trade back and forth; there is no hoard to draw on, yet commoners suffer at every turn.

sentences.zh: 且錢帛相半，爲制永久，或聞長宰須令輸直，進違舊科，退容姦利。

translations.literal: Moreover, half money and half silk was made a permanent rule; I hear that chief magistrates are made to demand cash payment, advancing in violation of the old statute and retreating to harbor illicit profit.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the permanent rule was half cash and half silk; I hear that magistrates are forced to demand cash alone, violating the old statute forward and profiting illicitly backward.

sentences.zh: :　　八屬近縣，旣在京畿，發借徵調，寔煩他邑，民特尤貧，連年失稔，草衣藿食，稍有流亡。

translations.literal: The eight districts' nearby counties, already within the capital zone; when requisitions and levies are issued, they truly burden other counties; the people are especially poor, for years failing harvest, clad in grass and eating wild greens, and some have fled.
translations.idiomatic: The eight districts near the capital lie within the metropolitan zone; when requisitions and levies go out, other counties are truly burdened—the people there are especially poor, harvests have failed for years, they wear grass and eat wild greens, and some have fled.

sentences.zh: 今農政就興，宜蒙賑給，若逋課未上，許以申原。

translations.literal: Now agricultural policy is to be revived; they ought to receive relief and sustenance; if arrears in tax have not been paid, let them be allowed to report and obtain remission.
translations.idiomatic: Now that farming is to be revived, they should receive relief; if tax arrears remain unpaid, let them report and obtain remission.

sentences.zh: :　　兖豫二藩，雖曰舊鎮，往屬兵虞，累弃鄉土。

translations.literal: The two domains of Yan and Yu are called old garrisons, yet in former times they belonged to military alarms and repeatedly abandoned their native soil.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Yu, though called old garrisons, have long known warfare and repeatedly lost their native lands.

sentences.zh: 密邇寇庭，下無安志。

translations.literal: Close to the enemy frontier, below there is no settled mind.
translations.idiomatic: Hard by the enemy frontier, the people below have no peace of mind.

sentences.zh: 編草結菴，不違凉暑；

translations.literal: Weaving grass into huts, not avoiding cold or heat;
translations.idiomatic: They weave grass into huts, braving cold and heat alike;

sentences.zh: 扶淮聚落，靡有生向。

translations.literal: Gathering settlements along the Huai, there is scarcely any will to live.
translations.idiomatic: Along the Huai they cluster in settlements with scarcely any will to live.

sentences.zh: 俱禀人靈，獨絕溫飽，而賦斂多少，尚均沃實。

translations.literal: All alike partake of human spirit, yet alone lack warmth and a full belly; yet the amount of levies and collections is still averaged against fertile, solid lands.
translations.idiomatic: They share the same human lot, yet alone lack warmth and full bellies—while levies are still assessed as if the land were rich and fertile.

sentences.zh: 謂凡在荒民，應加蠲減。

translations.literal: I hold that all destitute people in the wilderness should receive added remission and reduction.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that all destitute people in the frontier regions should receive added remissions.

sentences.zh: :　　又司市之要，自昔所難。

translations.literal: Moreover, the essentials of market supervision have since antiquity been difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the duties of market supervision have always been difficult.

sentences.zh: 頃來此役，不由才舉，竝條其重貲，許以賈衒。

translations.literal: In recent times this office has not been filled by talent; all are listed by heavy wealth and permitted to sell their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Recently these posts have not been filled by talent; candidates are ranked by wealth and permitted to buy office.

sentences.zh: 前人增估求俠，後人加稅請代，如此輪回，終何紀極？

translations.literal: Predecessors raised valuations and sought profit; successors added taxes and requested replacement—such rotation, when will it reach an end?
translations.idiomatic: Predecessors raised valuations to squeeze profit; successors added taxes and sought replacements—when will such rotation ever end?

sentences.zh: 兼復交關津要，共相脣齒，愚野未閑，必加陵誑，罪無大小，橫沒貲載。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the passes they associate like lip and teeth; the ignorant countryside, unversed in affairs, is surely subjected to intimidation and fraud; guilt great or small, goods are seized and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, officials at the passes collude like lip and teeth; ignorant country folk are surely cheated; regardless of guilt, goods are seized.

sentences.zh: 凡求試穀帛，類非廉謹，未解在事所以開容？

translations.literal: All who seek trial posts in grain and silk are by kind not upright and incorrupt—why are they indulged in office?
translations.idiomatic: Those who seek posts handling grain and silk are seldom upright—why are such men still indulged in office?

sentences.zh: :　　夫獄訟惟平，畫一在制，雖恩家得罪，必宜申憲，鼎姓貽諐，最合從網。

translations.literal: In lawsuits, fairness alone matters; uniformity lies in the regulations—though an enfeoffed house offends, it must still be judged by statute; though a tripod surname errs, it most fits the net.
translations.idiomatic: In lawsuits only fairness matters, and the law must be uniform—though a noble house offends, the statutes must be applied; though a great clan errs, the net must take them.

sentences.zh: 若罰典惟加賤下，辟書必蠲世族，懼非先王立理之本。

translations.literal: If punishments are applied only to the lowly while edicts of pardon always exempt noble clans, I fear this is not the foundation on which the former kings established order.
translations.idiomatic: If punishments fall only on the lowly while pardons always exempt noble clans, that is not how the sage kings of old founded good order.

sentences.zh: :　　尚書列曹，上應乾象。

translations.literal: Moreover, the bureaus of the Ministry of the Left correspond to the signs of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the ministry bureaus correspond to the signs of heaven.

sentences.zh: 如聞命議所出，先諮於都，都旣下意，然後付郎，謹寫關行。

translations.literal: I hear that wherever deliberations issue forth, they are first consulted at the capital; once the capital has set its intent, they are then handed to the clerks, who carefully write and transmit them.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that wherever policy deliberations originate, the capital is consulted first; once the capital has decided, the matter is handed to clerks who merely copy and transmit it.

sentences.zh: 愚謂郎官尤宜推擇。

translations.literal: I humbly hold that clerk officers especially ought to be chosen with care.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that clerks especially ought to be chosen with care.

sentences.zh: :　　宋運告終，戎車屢駕，寄名軍牒，動竊數等。

translations.literal: When the Song age reported its end, war chariots were repeatedly driven; names were attached to military registers, and ranks were stolen by several degrees.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song dynasty neared its end, campaigns were frequent; men borrowed names on military registers and stole several ranks.

sentences.zh: 故非分充朝，資奉殷積。

translations.literal: Thus those unqualified filled the court, and salaries and sustenance piled up richly.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the unqualified filled the court, and salaries piled up.

sentences.zh: 廣、越邦宰，梁、益郡邑，參差調補，寔允事機。

translations.literal: Prefects of Guang and Yue, administrators of Liang and Yi—adjusting and filling posts in due proportion truly suits the needs of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Posting governors to Guang and Yue and administrators to Liang and Yi, with assignments adjusted as needed, truly suits the times.

sentences.zh: 且此徒冗雜，罕遵王憲，嚴加廉視，隨違彈斥，一二年間，可減太半。

translations.literal: Moreover, this crowd is redundant and mixed, seldom obeying royal statutes; if strict integrity were applied in inspection, with violations reported and expelled, in the space of a year or two, more than half could be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, this crowd is redundant and seldom obeys the law; with strict oversight and dismissal for violations, within a year or two more than half could be cut.

sentences.zh: 五年，正位司徒，給班劔二十人，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he took the regular post of Minister of Education, was given twenty halberds of the guard, and remained Attendant at Court as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongming he became minister of education in full rank, was granted twenty guard halberds, and retained his post as attendant.

sentences.zh: 移居雞籠山邸，集學士抄《五經》、百家，依《皇覽》例爲《四部要略》千卷。

translations.literal: He moved his residence to the Jilong Mountain lodge, gathered scholars to copy the "Five Classics" and the hundred schools, and following the example of the "Imperial Overview" compiled the "Essential Digest of the Four Divisions" in a thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the Cock Cage Mountain estate, gathered scholars to copy the Five Classics and the hundred schools, and following the model of the Imperial Overview compiled the Essential Digest of the Four Divisions in a thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 招致名僧，講語佛法，造經唄新聲，道俗之盛，江左未有也。

translations.literal: He invited famous monks, lectured on Buddhist doctrine, and composed new scriptural chants; in the splendor of clergy and laity, the lower Yangtze had never seen the like.
translations.idiomatic: He invited eminent monks, expounded the Dharma, and composed new Buddhist chants; never had the lower Yangtze seen such splendor among clergy and laity.

sentences.zh: 世祖好射雉，子良諫曰：

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Qi loved shooting pheasants; Ziliang remonstrated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi loved hunting pheasant; Ziliang remonstrated as follows:

sentences.zh: :　　鑾轝亟動，天蹕屢巡，陵犯風煙，驅馳野澤。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage moves repeatedly, the heavenly escort patrols again and again, offending wind and mist, driving through wild marshes.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage moves again and again, the royal escort patrols repeatedly, braving wind and mist and racing through wild marshes.

sentences.zh: 萬乘至重，一羽甚微。

translations.literal: The ten-thousand chariot is supremely weighty; a single feather is exceedingly slight.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of ten thousand chariots is supremely weighty; a single feather is exceedingly slight.

sentences.zh: 從甚微之懽，忽至重之誡。

translations.literal: From the slightest pleasure, one suddenly forgets the supremely weighty warning.
translations.idiomatic: For the slightest sport one forgets the gravest warning.

sentences.zh: 頃郊郛以外，科禁嚴重，匪直芻牧事罷，遂乃窀掩殆廢。

translations.literal: Recently outside the suburbs and suburbs, statutes and prohibitions are severe; not only is pasturing and firewood ended, but burials are nearly abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Recently beyond the suburbs prohibitions are severe; not only pasturing and firewood are banned, but burials are nearly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 且田月向登，桑時告至，士女呼嗟，易生噂議，弃民從欲，理未可安。

translations.literal: Moreover, the farming month approaches harvest, the mulberry season announces its coming; men and women cry out, and slander easily arises; to abandon the people and follow one's desires—reason cannot approve it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, harvest and sericulture seasons are at hand; men and women cry out and slander easily arises; to abandon the people for one's pleasure cannot be justified.

sentences.zh: 曩時巡幸，必盡威防，領軍景先、詹事赤斧堅甲利兵，左右屯衞。

translations.literal: In former times on imperial tours, defenses were always complete; the Protector of the Army Jing Xian and the Household Master Chi Fu, in firm armor and sharp weapons, guarded left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly on imperial tours defenses were always complete; the Protector of the Army Jing Xian and the Household Master Chi Fu, in firm armor with sharp weapons, guarded left and right.

sentences.zh: 今馳騖外野，交侍疏闊，晨出晚還，頓遺清道，此實愚臣最所震迫。

translations.literal: Now galloping in the outer wilds, attendants sparse and loose, setting out at dawn and returning at dusk, suddenly leaving the cleared road—this is what your foolish servant most dreads.
translations.idiomatic: Now you gallop in the open country with a thin escort, leaving at dawn and returning at dusk and abandoning the cleared road—this is what I most dread.

sentences.zh: :　　狡虜玩威，甫獲款關，二漢全富，猶加曲待。

translations.literal: The crafty foe toys with our might; he has only just knocked at the passes in submission; when the two Han dynasties were wholly prosperous, they still treated him with special courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The northern foe tests our strength; he has only just submitted at the passes; even when the Han was wholly prosperous, envoys were treated with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 如聞使臣，頻亦怨望，前會東宮，遂形言色。

translations.literal: I hear that the envoys also frequently resent and complain; at the Eastern Palace they have already shown it in speech and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the envoys frequently resent their treatment; at the Eastern Palace they have already shown it in word and face.

sentences.zh: 昔宋氏遣使，舊列階下，劉纘銜使，始登朝殿。

translations.literal: Formerly the Song court sent envoys ranked below the steps; when Liu Zuan received the mission, they first ascended the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Song envoys were ranked below the steps; when Liu Zuan received the mission, they first ascended the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 今旣反命，宜賜優禮。

translations.literal: Now that they have returned with their commission, they ought to be granted generous ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Now that they have returned, they ought to receive generous ceremony.

sentences.zh: :　　伏謂中堂雲構，實惟峻絕，檐陛深嚴，事隔敘暑，而別爲一室，如或有疑。

translations.literal: I submit that the central hall, cloud-structured, is truly lofty and absolute; its eaves and steps are deeply solemn, affairs separated from the summer heat—and yet a separate room was made, as if there were doubt.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that the central hall, towering like clouds, is truly lofty; its eaves and steps are deeply solemn and keep out the summer heat—yet a separate room was built, as if there were doubt.

sentences.zh: 邊帶廣途，訛言孔熾，毀立之易，過於轉圓，若依舊制通敞，實允觀聽。

translations.literal: Along the broad roads at the borders, false talk blazes fiercely; to destroy or establish is easier than turning a wheel; if the old system of openness were restored, it would truly satisfy sight and hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Along the broad roads slander runs wild; to tear down or build is easier than turning a wheel; if the old open design were restored, it would truly satisfy public opinion.

sentences.zh: :　　頃市司驅扇，租估過刻，吹毛求瑕，廉察相繼，被以小罪，責以重備。

translations.literal: Recently market officers have driven and fanned prices, rent assessments overly harsh, picking hairs for flaws, integrity inspections following in succession; for a small offense one is charged heavy compensation.
translations.idiomatic: Recently market officers have driven up prices, rent assessments are overly harsh, and inspectors pick at every flaw; for a small offense one is charged heavy compensation.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜勑有司，更詳優格。

translations.literal: I humbly hold that the relevant offices ought to be ordered to set more lenient standards in detail.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that the relevant offices should be ordered to set more lenient standards.

sentences.zh: :　　臣年方朝賢，齒未相及，以管窺天，猶知失得，廊廟之士，豈闇是非。

translations.literal: Your servant's years match those at court, my teeth have not yet caught up; viewing heaven through a tube, I still know gain and loss—the gentlemen of the court, how could they be blind to right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: I am still young among court worthies and have not yet reached their years; viewing heaven through a tube, I still know gain from loss—can the gentlemen of the court be blind to right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 未聞一人開一說爲陛下憂國家，非但面從，亦畏威耳。

translations.literal: I have not heard a single man open a single proposal to worry on the state's behalf for Your Majesty; they not only agree to your face but also fear your majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I have not heard a single man speak openly for the state's sake; they not only agree to your face but also fear your majesty.

sentences.zh: 臣若不啓，陛下於何聞之？

translations.literal: If your servant does not speak, through what will Your Majesty hear it?
translations.idiomatic: If I do not speak, how will Your Majesty hear of it?

sentences.zh: 先是六年，左衞、殿中將軍邯鄲超上書諫射雉，世祖爲止。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the sixth year, Left Guards and Palace Army General Handan Chao submitted a memorial remonstrating against pheasant shooting, and Emperor Wu of Qi ceased it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the sixth year, Left Guards and Palace Army general Handan Chao memorialized against pheasant hunting, and Emperor Wu of Qi stopped.

sentences.zh: 久之，超竟被誅。

translations.literal: After a long time, Chao was in the end executed.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while, Chao was in the end executed.

sentences.zh: 永明末，上將射雉。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongming, the emperor was about to shoot pheasant.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yongming era, the emperor was about to hunt pheasant again.

sentences.zh: 子良諫曰：

translations.literal: Ziliang remonstrated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang remonstrated as follows:

sentences.zh: :　　忽聞外議，伏承當更射雉。

translations.literal: Suddenly I hear outside talk; I bow to learn that you intend again to shoot pheasant.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly I hear outside talk; I learn that you intend again to hunt pheasant.

sentences.zh: 臣下情震越，心懷憂悚，猶謂疑妄，事不必然。

translations.literal: Below, my feelings are shaken and overset; in my heart I am anxious and fearful; I still say it is doubtful and false, that the affair cannot be real.
translations.idiomatic: My feelings below are shaken with dread; in my heart I am anxious and fearful; I still hope it is rumor and that the matter cannot be real.

sentences.zh: 伏度陛下以信心明照，所以傾金寶於禪靈，仁愛廣洽，得使禽魚養命於江澤，豈惟國慶民懽，乃以翱翔治樂。

translations.literal: I bow to measure that Your Majesty, with faith and bright illumination, therefore poured gold and treasure at Chanling, with benevolence broadly harmonizing, so that birds and fish may preserve life in rivers and marshes—not only the state's felicity and the people's joy, but even soaring and roaming find governance and delight.
translations.idiomatic: I trust that Your Majesty, with faith and luminous wisdom, poured gold and treasure at Chanling and with broad benevolence let birds and fish live in rivers and marshes—not only bringing the state joy and the people happiness, but even in flight and roaming showing humane rule.

sentences.zh: 夫衞生保命，人獸不殊；

translations.literal: To guard life and preserve the body, men and beasts are not different;
translations.idiomatic: To preserve life and guard the body, men and beasts are alike;

sentences.zh: 重軀愛體，彼我無異。

translations.literal: To value the body and love the person, between them and us there is no difference.
translations.idiomatic: To cherish body and life, between them and us there is no difference.

sentences.zh: 故禮云「聞其聲不食其肉，見其生不忍其死」。

translations.literal: Thus the Rites say, "Hearing its voice, one does not eat its flesh; seeing it alive, one cannot bear its death."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Rites say, "Hearing its voice, one does not eat its flesh; seeing it alive, one cannot bear its death."

sentences.zh: 且萬乘之尊，降同匹夫之樂，夭殺無辜，傷仁害福之本。

translations.literal: Moreover, the honor of ten thousand chariots descends to the pleasure of a common man; killing the innocent injures the root of benevolence and blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, for the ruler of ten thousand chariots to descend to a commoner's sport, killing the innocent injures the root of benevolence and blessing.

sentences.zh: 菩薩不殺，壽命得長。

translations.literal: The bodhisattva does not kill, and life is thereby long.
translations.idiomatic: When the bodhisattva refrains from killing, life is lengthened.

sentences.zh: 施物安樂，自無恐怖。

translations.literal: Giving things brings peace and joy; of itself there is no terror.
translations.idiomatic: Giving brings peace and joy; of itself there is no terror.

sentences.zh: 不惱衆生，身無患苦。

translations.literal: Not troubling living beings, the body has no affliction.
translations.idiomatic: When one does not trouble living beings, the body knows no affliction.

sentences.zh: 臣見功德有此果報，所以日夜劬懃，厲身奉法，實願聖躬康御若此。

translations.literal: Your servant sees that merit has this fruit and retribution; therefore day and night I am diligent, disciplining my person to uphold the law, truly wishing the sacred person may be well and governed like this.
translations.idiomatic: I see that merit brings such reward; therefore day and night I am diligent, disciplining myself to uphold the law, truly wishing Your Majesty health and governance like this.

sentences.zh: 每至寢夢，脫有異見，不覺身心立就燋爛。

translations.literal: Whenever I reach sleep and dreams, if suddenly there is a strange sight, without noticing, body and mind at once become scorched and burned.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I dream, if something strange appears, my body and mind feel at once scorched.

sentences.zh: 陛下常日捨財脩福，臣私心顒顒，尚恨其少，豈可今日有見此事？

translations.literal: Your Majesty on ordinary days gives up wealth to cultivate merit; in my private heart I am earnest and still regret it is little—how can today there be this sight of the affair?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty on ordinary days gives up wealth to cultivate merit; in my private heart I am earnest and still regret it is too little—how can today there be such a thing?

sentences.zh: 一損福業，追悔便難。

translations.literal: Once merit is damaged, repentance afterward is hard.
translations.idiomatic: Once merit is damaged, repentance is hard.

sentences.zh: 臣此啓聞，私心實切。

translations.literal: Your servant, on hearing this memorial, in private heart is truly urgent.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this memorial, my private heart is truly urgent.

sentences.zh: 若是大事，不可易改，亦願陛下照臣此誠，曲垂三思。

translations.literal: If it is a great matter, it cannot be lightly changed; I also wish Your Majesty to reflect upon this sincerity of mine and bend to grant threefold consideration.
translations.idiomatic: If it is a great matter, it cannot be lightly changed; I also ask Your Majesty to heed this sincerity of mine and grant it threefold reconsideration.

sentences.zh: 況此嬉遊之閒，非關當否，而動輙傷生，實可深慎。

translations.literal: Moreover this is the leisure of play and amusement, not bearing on right or wrong, yet each move often injures life—it truly may be deeply cautioned.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover this is mere sport and diversion, unrelated to right or wrong, yet each move often costs lives; it truly calls for the deepest caution.

sentences.zh: :　　臣聞子孝奉君，臣忠事主，莫不靈祇通感，徵祥證登。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that a filial son in serving his lord and a loyal minister in serving his master—none fail to have spirits and deities respond in communion, with auspicious omens attesting and ascending.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that when sons are filial in serving their lord and ministers loyal in serving their master, spirits and deities respond in communion, and auspicious signs bear witness on high.

sentences.zh: 臣近段仰啓，賜希受戒，天心洞遠，誠未達勝善之途，而聖恩遲疑，尚未垂履曲降尊極，豈可今月復隨此事？

translations.literal: Your servant recently, looking up, memorialized, beseeching to receive the precepts; the mind of Heaven is profound and far, and I truly have not reached the path of supreme goodness, yet the sage grace hesitated and delayed, and has not yet bent to tread down and lower the utmost dignity—how can this month again follow this affair?
translations.idiomatic: Your servant recently memorialized, begging to receive the precepts; the mind of Heaven is profound and far, and I have not yet attained the path of supreme goodness, yet imperial grace still hesitates and has not bent to descend from the highest dignity—how can this month again follow such an affair?

sentences.zh: 臣不隱心，卽實上啓。

translations.literal: Your servant does not hide the heart; forthwith truly memorializing upward.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant conceals nothing in his heart and now reports it in full.

sentences.zh: 雖不盡納，而深見寵愛。

translations.literal: Although not all was adopted, yet he deeply saw favor and affection.
translations.idiomatic: Although not everything was adopted, he was still shown deep favor and affection.

sentences.zh: 又與文惠太子同好釋氏，甚相友悌。

translations.literal: Moreover he shared a liking for the Buddhist school with Crown Prince Wenhui, and they were very friendly and fraternal.
translations.idiomatic: He also shared a devotion to Buddhism with Crown Prince Wenhui, and the two were deeply friendly and fraternal.

sentences.zh: 子良敬信尤篤，數於邸園營齋戒，大集朝臣衆僧，至於賦食行水，或躬親其事，世頗以爲失宰相體。

translations.literal: Ziliang's reverent faith was especially devout; several times at his mansion garden he held fasts and precepts, greatly gathering court ministers and multitudes of monks, even to distributing food and serving water, sometimes personally undertaking these affairs—the age largely considered this a loss of a chief minister's dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang's reverent faith was especially deep; he often held fasts and precepts at his mansion gardens, gathering great assemblies of court ministers and monks, even distributing food and pouring water himself at times, which many in the age thought unbecoming of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 勸人爲善，未嘗厭倦，以此終致盛名。

translations.literal: In urging people toward goodness he never grew weary; by this he ultimately attained great renown.
translations.idiomatic: In urging others toward goodness he never wearied, and by this he ultimately won great renown.

sentences.zh: 尋代王儉領國子祭酒，辭不拜。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Wang Jian as Director of the Imperial University but declined to accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was to replace Wang Jian as Director of the Imperial University, but he declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 八年，給三望車。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was given a three-canopied carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was granted a three-canopied carriage.

sentences.zh: 九年，京邑大水，吳興偏劇，子良開倉賑救貧病不能立者，於第北立廨收養，給衣及藥。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the capital region suffered great flood; Wuxing was especially severe. Ziliang opened his granaries to relieve and save those poor and ill who could not stand; north of his residence he established an office to receive and foster them, providing clothes and medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the capital was inundated and Wuxing was especially hard hit; Ziliang opened his granaries to aid the poor and sick who could not rise, set up a shelter north of his mansion to take them in, and supplied clothing and medicine.

sentences.zh: 十年，領尚書令。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he served as Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he served as Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋爲使持節、都督揚州諸軍事、揚州刺史，本官如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commissioner commanding all military affairs of Yang Province, and Governor of Yang Province; his original posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commissioner over all military affairs of Yang Province, and Governor of Yang Province, while retaining his existing offices.

sentences.zh: 尋解尚書令，加中書監。

translations.literal: Soon he was relieved of Director of the Imperial Secretariat and promoted to Supervisor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he relinquished the directorship of the Secretariat and was made Supervisor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子薨，世祖檢行東宮，見太子服御羽儀，多過制度，上大怒，以子良與太子善，不啓聞，頗加嫌責。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Wenhui died, Emperor Wu inspected the Eastern Palace and saw the prince's apparel and insignia of feathers and banners mostly exceeded regulations; the emperor was greatly angered. Because Ziliang had been close to the prince and had not reported it, he was considerably blamed and censured.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Wenhui died, Emperor Wu inspected the Eastern Palace and found the prince's raiment and feathered banners far beyond regulation; the emperor was furious. Because Ziliang had been close to the prince and had not reported it, he was sharply blamed and censured.

sentences.zh: 世祖不豫，詔子良甲仗入延昌殿侍醫藥。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu fell ill, an edict ordered Ziliang, in armor and with weapons, to enter Yanqing Hall to attend to medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu fell ill, an edict ordered Ziliang, armed and in armor, to enter Yanqing Hall to attend his medical care.

sentences.zh: 子良啓進沙門於殿戶前誦經，世祖爲感夢見優曇缽華，子良按佛經宣旨使御府以銅爲華，插御牀四角。

translations.literal: Ziliang memorialized recommending monks to chant sutras before the hall doors. Emperor Wu was moved to dream of the udumbara flower. Ziliang, following Buddhist scripture, proclaimed the imperial will and had the palace workshop fashion flowers of bronze to place at the four corners of the imperial couch.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang memorialized that monks be brought to chant sutras before the hall doors; Emperor Wu was moved to dream of the udumbara flower, and Ziliang, citing scripture, had the imperial workshop cast bronze flowers and set them at the four corners of the imperial couch.

sentences.zh: 日夜在殿內，太孫閒日入參承。

translations.literal: Day and night he was in the hall; on leisure days the heir would enter to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: He remained in the hall day and night, while on free days the heir would enter to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 世祖暴漸，內外惶懼，百僚皆已變服，物議立子良，俄頃而蘇，問太孫所在，因召東宮器甲皆入。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu's illness suddenly worsened. Within and without there was fear; all officials had already changed to mourning dress. Public discussion favored installing Ziliang. In a moment he revived and asked where the heir was; thereupon he summoned the Eastern Palace's weapons and armor to be brought in.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's illness suddenly worsened; inside and outside the palace there was panic, and all officials had already changed into mourning dress while public talk favored enthroning Ziliang. In a moment he revived, asked where the heir was, and ordered the Eastern Palace's arms and armor brought in.

sentences.zh: 遺詔使子良輔政，高宗知尚書事。

translations.literal: The testamentary edict made Ziliang assist in government, and Emperor Ming (Xiao Luan) oversee Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The deathbed edict made Ziliang assist in government and Emperor Ming (Xiao Luan) oversee Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 子良素仁厚，不樂世務，乃推高宗。

translations.literal: Ziliang was by nature benevolent and generous and took no joy in worldly affairs; he thus yielded to Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang was by nature benevolent and took no pleasure in worldly affairs, and so he yielded the lead to Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 詔云：「事無大小，悉與鸞參懷。

translations.literal: The edict said: "In affairs great or small, all are to be deliberated with Luan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "In affairs great or small, all shall be deliberated with Luan.

sentences.zh: 」子良所志也。

translations.literal: " This was Ziliang's wish.
translations.idiomatic: This was what Ziliang had wished for.

sentences.zh: 太孫少養於子良妃袁氏，甚著慈愛，旣懼前不得立，自此深忌子良。

translations.literal: The heir had been raised from childhood by Ziliang's consort, Lady Yuan; affection was very marked. Having feared beforehand that he would not be established, from this time he deeply resented Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: The heir had been raised from childhood by Ziliang's consort, Lady Yuan, and affection between them was evident; having feared earlier that he might not succeed, from this time he deeply resented Ziliang.

sentences.zh: 大行出太極殿，子良居中書省，帝使虎賁中郎將潘敞領二百人仗屯太極西階防之。

translations.literal: When the late emperor's coffin left the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, Ziliang was at the Central Secretariat. The emperor sent Rapid-as-Tiger Guards Commandant Pan Chang leading two hundred men with weapons to garrison the western steps of Supreme Ultimate to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor's coffin left the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, Ziliang remained at the Central Secretariat; the emperor sent Rapid-as-Tiger Guards Commandant Pan Chang with two hundred armed men to hold the western steps of Supreme Ultimate and guard against him.

sentences.zh: 成服後，諸王皆出，子良乞停至山陵，不許。

translations.literal: After the mourning garments were completed, all the princes departed; Ziliang begged to remain until the mountain tomb but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period was completed, all the princes left the capital; Ziliang begged to remain until the imperial tomb was finished, but permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 進位太傅，增班劔爲三十人，本官如故。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Tutor; his ceremonial guard was increased to thirty; his original posts remained.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Tutor, his ceremonial guard increased to thirty men, and his other offices remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 解侍中。

translations.literal: He was relieved of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was relieved of the post of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: ，加殊禮，劔履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名。

translations.literal: He was granted extraordinary honors: sword and shoes in the hall, no need to hasten when entering court, and no personal name called when praised in obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted extraordinary honors: he might wear sword and shoes in the hall, need not hasten when entering court, and his personal name was not called when he was praised in obeisance.

sentences.zh: 進督南徐州。

translations.literal: He was advanced to supervise South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed to supervise South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 其年疾篤，謂左右曰：「門外應有異。

translations.literal: That year his illness was grave. He said to those beside him: "Outside the gate there should be something strange.
translations.idiomatic: That year his illness grew grave, and he said to those beside him, "There should be something strange outside the gate."

sentences.zh: 」遣人視，見淮中魚萬數，皆浮出水上向城門。

translations.literal: " He sent men to look and saw tens of thousands of fish in the Huai, all floating up on the water toward the city gate.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men to look and saw tens of thousands of fish in the Huai River floating to the surface and drifting toward the city gate.

sentences.zh: 尋薨，時年三十五。

translations.literal: Soon he died, aged thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died, at the age of thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 帝常慮子良有異志，及薨，甚悅。

translations.literal: The emperor had often feared Ziliang harbored a different intent; when he died, he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long feared that Ziliang harbored a rival ambition, and when he died the emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 詔給東園溫明秘器，斂以袞冕之服。

translations.literal: An edict granted the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden and Warm Brightness; he was enshrouded in robes of the highest ceremonial rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted the secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden and Warm Brightness, and he was laid out in the robes of supreme ceremonial rank.

sentences.zh: 東府施喪位，大鴻臚持節監護，太官朝夕送祭。

translations.literal: The Eastern Mansion set up mourning stations; the Grand Herald, bearing the staff, supervised; the Imperial Kitchen morning and evening sent offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning stations were set up at the Eastern Mansion; the Grand Herald, bearing the staff of authority, supervised the rites, and the Imperial Kitchen sent offerings morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「褒崇明德，前王令典，追遠尊親，沿情所隆。
