translations.literal: Again an edict said: "To praise and uplift bright virtue is the worthy statute of former kings; to follow the distant and honor kin is what feeling along custom uplifts.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, "To praise and exalt bright virtue is the worthy statute of former kings; to honor the distant dead and revere kin is what feeling along custom elevates."

sentences.zh: 故使持節、都督揚州諸軍事、中書監、太傅、領司徒、揚州刺史、竟陵王、新除督南徐州，體睿履正，神鑒淵邈。

translations.literal: The late Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commissioner commanding all military affairs of Yang Province, Supervisor of the Central Secretariat, Grand Tutor, concurrent Minister of Education, Governor of Yang Province, Prince of Jingling, newly appointed to supervise South Xuzhou—his bodily substance was wise, his tread upright, his spirit discernment deep and far.
translations.idiomatic: The late Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commissioner over all military affairs of Yang Province, Supervisor of the Central Secretariat, Grand Tutor, concurrent Minister of Education, Governor of Yang Province, Prince of Jingling, and newly appointed supervisor of South Xuzhou—his person was wise, his conduct upright, and his spiritual discernment profound and far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 道冠民宗，具瞻允集。

translations.literal: His Way crowned the people's ancestor; all who looked to him gathered in trust.
translations.idiomatic: His virtue crowned the people's exemplar, and all eyes turned to him in trust.

sentences.zh: 肇自弱齡，孝友光備。

translations.literal: From his tender years, filial piety and brotherly friendship shone complete.
translations.idiomatic: From his youth, filial piety and brotherly affection shone complete.

sentences.zh: 爰及贊契，協升景業。

translations.literal: Reaching to his assisting the bond, he joined in ascending the bright enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to assist the founding bond, he joined in raising the bright enterprise.

sentences.zh: 燮曜台陛，五教克宣。

translations.literal: He harmonized and illumined the terrace steps; the five teachings were fully proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: He harmonized and illumined the court, and the five teachings were fully proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 敷奏朝端，百揆惟穆。

translations.literal: He laid out memorials at the court's head; the hundred duties were only harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: He presented policy at the head of court, and the hundred offices were harmonious.

sentences.zh: 寄重先顧，任均負圖。

translations.literal: Entrusted with weight in the former regard, his charge equaled bearing the chart.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with weight in the founding care, his burden equaled bearing the realm's chart.

sentences.zh: 諒以齊暉《二南》，同規往哲。

translations.literal: Truly he aligned the splendor of the "Two Souths" with the same measure as sages of old.
translations.idiomatic: Truly he matched the radiance of the "Two Souths" and shared the measure of sages of old.

sentences.zh: 方憑保祐，永翼雍熙。

translations.literal: Just then relying on his preservation and aid, forever winging flourishing peace.
translations.idiomatic: We had relied on his protection to wing enduring prosperity.

sentences.zh: 天不憖遺，奄焉薨逝。

translations.literal: Heaven did not pity and preserve him; suddenly he passed away in death.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven did not spare him, and suddenly he passed away.

sentences.zh: 哀慕抽割，震于厥心。

translations.literal: Grief and longing tore and cut; it shook his very heart.
translations.idiomatic: Grief and longing tear at the heart and shake it to the core.

sentences.zh: 今龜謀襲吉，先遠戒期。

translations.literal: Now the tortoise divination inherits auspice; the distant forebear sets the warning date.
translations.idiomatic: Now the tortoise divination has yielded an auspicious day, and the time for honoring the departed draws near.

sentences.zh: 宜崇嘉制，式弘風烈。

translations.literal: It is fitting to uplift the excellent ordinance and thereby expand the wind of lofty deeds.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to exalt him with honorable rites and thereby magnify his exemplary renown.

sentences.zh: 可追崇假黃鉞、侍中、都督中外諸軍事、太宰、領大將軍、揚州牧，綠綟綬，備九服錫命之禮。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously exalted with the provisional yellow battle-axe, Palace Attendant, Commissioner over all military affairs within and without, Grand Minister, concurrent Grand General, Governor of Yang Province, green ribbon and seal-cord, and furnished with the nine gifts and investiture rites.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously honored with the provisional yellow battle-axe, Palace Attendant, Commissioner over all military affairs at home and abroad, Grand Minister, concurrent Grand General, Governor of Yang Province, the green ribbon and seal-cord, and the full nine gifts of investiture.

sentences.zh: 使持節、中書監、王如故。

translations.literal: Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Supervisor of the Central Secretariat—the prince's offices remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: His offices as Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Supervisor of the Central Secretariat shall remain as before.

sentences.zh: 給九旒鸞輅，黃屋左纛，轀輬車，前後部羽葆鼓吹，輓歌二部，虎賁班劔百人，葬禮依晉安平王孚故事。

translations.literal: Grant the nine tassels and phoenix carriage, yellow canopy with left banner, covered transport carriage, front and rear sections with feathered parasols and martial music, two sections of dirge singers, one hundred Rapid-as-Tiger ceremonial guards, and funeral rites following the precedent of Jin's Prince of Pingyang, Sima Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Grant the nine-tasseled phoenix carriage, yellow canopy with left banner, covered transport carriage, front and rear escorts with feathered parasols and martial music, two sections of dirge singers, one hundred Rapid-as-Tiger ceremonial guards, and funeral rites following the precedent of Jin's Prince of Pingyang, Sima Fu.

sentences.zh: 」初，豫章王嶷葬金牛山，文惠太子葬夾石，子良臨送，望祖硎山，悲感歎曰：「北瞻吾叔，前望吾兄，死而有知，請葬茲地。

translations.literal: Earlier, Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Liao was buried at Golden Ox Mountain and Crown Prince Wenhui at Jia Rock. When Ziliang attended the send-off and gazed toward Ancestor's Whetstone Mountain, he grieved and sighed: "Looking north I see my uncle; looking ahead I see my brother—if the dead have awareness, let me be buried in this place.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Liao had been buried at Golden Ox Mountain and Crown Prince Wenhui at Jia Rock; when Ziliang attended the funeral and gazed toward Ancestor's Whetstone Mountain, he grieved and said, "To the north I see my uncle, before me my brother—if the dead have awareness, let me be buried here."

sentences.zh: 」旣薨，遂葬焉。

translations.literal: " When he died, he was indeed buried there.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was buried there as he had wished.

sentences.zh: 所著內外文筆數十卷，雖無文采，多是勸戒。

translations.literal: Literary writings inner and outer that he composed number several tens of scrolls; although without literary polish, most are admonitions and warnings.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings, inner and outer, number several tens of scrolls; though without literary polish, most are admonitions and warnings.

sentences.zh: 建武中，故吏范雲上表爲子良立碑，事不行。

translations.literal: During the Jianwu period, his former subordinate Fan Yun memorialized to erect a stele for Ziliang; the matter was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwu period, his former subordinate Fan Yun submitted a memorial to erect a stele for Ziliang, but the proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 子昭冑嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhaochou succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhaochou succeeded him.

translations.literal: Section divider in the source text.

sentences.zh: 子 昭冑

translations.literal: Son Zhaochou
translations.idiomatic: Son Zhaochou

sentences.zh: =昭冑字景胤。

translations.literal: Zhaochou, styled name Jingyin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaochou, courtesy name Jingyin.

sentences.zh: 汎涉有父風。

translations.literal: Broadly versed, he had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned, he bore his father's manner.

sentences.zh: ，自竟陵王世子爲寧朔將軍、會稽太守。

translations.literal: From heir of the Prince of Jingling he became General of Pacifying the North and Governor of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: From heir of the Prince of Jingling he became General of Pacifying the North and Governor of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 鬱林初，爲右衞將軍，未拜，遷侍中，領右軍將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yulin reign he was made General of the Right Guard but had not yet received the appointment when he was transferred to Palace Attendant and concurrent General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yulin reign he was appointed General of the Right Guard; before he could take up the post he was transferred to Palace Attendant and concurrent General of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 建武三年，復爲侍中，領驍騎將軍，轉散騎常侍，太常。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianwu he again became Palace Attendant and concurrent General of Valiant Cavalry, then transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianwu he again became Palace Attendant and concurrent General of Valiant Cavalry, then was transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 以封境邊虜，永元元年，改封巴陵王。

translations.literal: Because his fief bordered barbarian lands, in the first year of Yongyuan he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Because his fief bordered foreign territory, in the first year of Yongyuan he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Baling.

sentences.zh: 先是王敬則事起，南康侯子恪在吳郡，高宗慮有同異，召諸王侯入宮。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Jingze's affair arose, Marquis of Nankang Zike was in Wu Commandery; Emperor Ming feared disloyalty and summoned all princes and marquises into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wang Jingze's rebellion broke out, Marquis of Nankang Zike was in Wu Commandery; Emperor Ming feared disloyalty among the princes and summoned all kings and marquises into the palace.

sentences.zh: 晉安王寶義及江陵公寶覽等住中書省，高、武諸孫住西省，勑人各兩左右自隨，過此依軍法，孩抱者乳母隨入。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin'an Bao Yi and Duke of Jiangling Bao Lan and others lodged in the Central Secretariat; the grandsons of the Gao and Wu emperors lodged in the Western Secretariat. An order allowed each man only two attendants of his own; beyond that military law applied, and infants in arms were admitted only with wet nurses.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin'an Bao Yi, Duke of Jiangling Bao Lan, and others were lodged in the Central Secretariat, while the grandsons of Emperors Gao and Wu were lodged in the Western Secretariat; each man was allowed only two personal attendants, and beyond that military law applied—infants in arms might enter only with their wet nurses.

sentences.zh: 其夜太醫煮藥，都水辦數十具棺材，須三更當悉殺之。

translations.literal: That night the imperial physicians brewed medicine, the Directorate of Waterways prepared several tens of coffins, and at the third watch all were to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: That night the imperial physicians brewed medicine, the Directorate of Waterways prepared dozens of coffins, and at the third watch all were to be killed.

sentences.zh: 子恪奔歸，二更達建陽門刺啓。

translations.literal: Zike fled back; at the second watch he reached Jianyang Gate and submitted an urgent report.
translations.idiomatic: Zike fled back to the capital and at the second watch reached Jianyang Gate with an urgent report.

sentences.zh: 時刻已至，而帝眠不起，中書舍人沈徽孚與帝所親左右單景雋共謀少留其事，須臾帝覺，景雋啓子恪已至，驚問曰：「未邪？

translations.literal: The hour had already come, yet the emperor slept and would not rise. Secretariat Attendant Shen Huifu and the emperor's intimate attendant Shan Jingjun together plotted to delay the affair a little. In a moment the emperor awoke; Jingjun reported that Zike had arrived, and startled he asked: "Not yet?
translations.idiomatic: The hour had come, yet the emperor still slept and would not rise; Secretariat Attendant Shen Huifu and the emperor's intimate attendant Shan Jingjun plotted together to delay the matter a little. Presently the emperor awoke; Jingjun reported that Zike had arrived, and the emperor asked in alarm, "Not yet?"

sentences.zh: 」景雋具以事荅。

translations.literal: " Jingjun fully reported the affair in answer.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjun reported the whole affair in detail.

sentences.zh: 明日悉遣王侯還第。

translations.literal: The next day all the kings and marquises were sent back to their mansions.
translations.idiomatic: The next day all the princes and marquises were sent back to their residences.

sentences.zh: 建武以來，高、武王侯居常震怖，朝不保夕，至是尤甚。

translations.literal: Since Jianwu, the kings and marquises of the Gao and Wu lines had constantly lived in terror, not sure of surviving from morning to evening; at this time it was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jianwu period the princes and marquises of the Gao and Wu lines had lived in constant terror, unsure from morning to evening whether they would survive; now their fear was especially acute.

sentences.zh: 及陳顯達起事，王侯復入宮。

translations.literal: When Chen Xianda raised an affair, the kings and marquises again entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Xianda rose in rebellion, the princes and marquises were again summoned into the palace.

sentences.zh: 昭冑懲往時之懼，與弟永新侯昭穎逃奔江西，變形爲道人。

translations.literal: Zhaochou, chastened by fear of former times, fled with his younger brother, Marquis of Yongxin Zhaoying, to the lands west of the river and changed their forms to become Daoist priests.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaochou, remembering his earlier terror, fled with his younger brother, Marquis of Yongxin Zhaoying, to the region west of the Yangzi and disguised themselves as Daoist priests.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景舉兵，昭冑兄弟出投之。

translations.literal: When Cui Huijing raised troops, the Zhaochou brothers went out to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Huijing raised troops, the Zhaochou brothers went out to join him.

sentences.zh: 慧景事敗，昭冑兄弟首出投臺軍主胡松，各以王侯還第。

translations.literal: When Huijing's affair failed, the Zhaochou brothers were first to come out and submit to the capital army commander Hu Song; each was sent back to his mansion as king or marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When Huijing's rebellion failed, the Zhaochou brothers were the first to surrender to the capital army commander Hu Song and were each sent back to his residence with his title restored.

sentences.zh: 不自安，謀爲身計。

translations.literal: Not at ease in themselves, they plotted for their own preservation.
translations.idiomatic: Still uneasy, they plotted to secure their own safety.

sentences.zh: 子良故防閤桑偃爲梅蟲兒軍副，結前巴西太守蕭寅，謀立昭冑。

translations.literal: Ziliang's former guard-commander Sang Yan served as deputy to Mei Chong'er's army and joined with the former Governor of Baxi Xiao Yin to plot enthroning Zhaochou.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang's former guard-commander Sang Yan, deputy in Mei Chong'er's army, joined with the former Governor of Baxi Xiao Yin in a plot to enthrone Zhaochou.

sentences.zh: 昭冑許事克用寅爲尚書左僕射、護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Zhaochou promised that if the affair succeeded he would use Yin as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaochou promised that if the plot succeeded he would appoint Yin Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 以寅有部曲，大事皆委之。

translations.literal: Because Yin had a private following, all great affairs were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yin commanded his own troops, all major matters were entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 時胡松領軍在新亭，寅遣人說之，云「須昏人出，寅等便率兵奉昭冑入臺，閉城號令。

translations.literal: At that time Hu Song commanded the army at Xinting; Yin sent men to persuade him, saying: "When the dim emperor comes out, Yin and the rest will at once lead troops to escort Zhaochou into the palace platform, close the city, and issue commands.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hu Song commanded the army at Xinting; Yin sent men to win him over, saying, "When Emperor Donghun comes out, we shall at once lead troops to escort Zhaochou into the palace, close the city gates, and issue our commands."

sentences.zh: 昏人必還就將軍，將軍但閉壘不應，則三公不足得也。

translations.literal: The dim emperor will certainly return to seek the general; the general need only close the ramparts and not respond, and then the Three Excellencies cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor will certainly return to you; if you only close your ramparts and do not respond, then the Three Excellencies cannot touch you."

sentences.zh: 」松又許諾。

translations.literal: " Song again promised agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Song again gave his promise.

sentences.zh: 會東昏新起芳樂苑，月許日不復出遊，偃等議募健兒百餘人從萬春門入突取之，昭冑以爲不可。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Donghun had newly built the Garden of Fragrant Delights and for a month or so did not go out again on excursions; Yan and the rest discussed recruiting more than a hundred stalwart men to enter through Wanchun Gate and seize him in a surprise attack, but Zhaochou thought it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Emperor Donghun had newly built the Garden of Fragrant Delights and for a month or so did not go out on excursions; Yan and his fellows discussed recruiting more than a hundred stalwart men to burst in through Wanchun Gate and seize him, but Zhaochou thought it unwise.

sentences.zh: 偃同黨王山沙慮事久無成，以事告御刀徐僧重。

translations.literal: Yan's fellow conspirator Wang Shansha, fearing the affair long without success, reported it to Imperial Blade Attendant Xu Sengzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's fellow conspirator Wang Shansha, fearing the plot would never succeed, reported the affair to Imperial Blade Attendant Xu Sengzhong.

sentences.zh: 寅遣人殺山沙於路，吏於麝中得其事迹，昭冑兄弟與同黨皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Yin sent men to kill Shansha on the road, but officials found the account of the affair in his musk pouch; the Zhaochou brothers and all fellow conspirators were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sent men to kill Shansha on the road, but officials found the written account of the plot in his musk pouch; the Zhaochou brothers and all their fellow conspirators were executed.

sentences.zh: 昭穎官至寧朔將軍、彭城太守。

translations.literal: Zhaoying rose to General of Pacifying the North and Governor of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoying rose to the rank of General of Pacifying the North and Governor of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 梁王定京邑，追贈昭冑散騎常侍、撫軍將軍，昭穎黃門郎。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Liang secured the capital region, Zhaochou was posthumously honored as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Pacifies the Army, and Zhaoying as Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Liang secured the capital, Zhaochou was posthumously honored as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Pacifies the Army, and Zhaoying as Yellow Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 梁受禪，降封昭冑子周監利侯。

translations.literal: When Liang received the abdication, Zhaochou's son Zhou was demoted and enfeoffed as Marquis of Jianli.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang dynasty received the abdication, Zhaochou's son Zhou was demoted to Marquis of Jianli.

sentences.zh: 廬陵王子卿

translations.literal: Prince of Luling Ziqing
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Luling Ziqing

sentences.zh: 廬陵王子卿字雲長，世祖第三子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Luling Ziqing, styled name Yunchang, was the third son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Luling Ziqing, courtesy name Yunchang, was the third son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，封臨汝縣公，千五百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as Duke of Linru with one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as Duke of Linru with a fief of one thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 兄弟四人同封。

translations.literal: Four brothers were enfeoffed together.
translations.idiomatic: Four brothers received enfeoffment together.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，爲持節、都督郢州司州之義陽軍事、冠軍將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he became Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over the military affairs of Ying Province and Yiyang in Sizhou, General of the Champions, and Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over the military affairs of Ying Province and Yiyang in Sizhou, General of the Champions, and Governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: ，徙都督荊湘益寧梁南北秦七州、安西將軍、荊州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner over the seven provinces Jing, Xiang, Yi, Ning, Liang, and North and South Qin, General of Pacifying the West, and Governor of Jing Province; Bearer of the Staff remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Commissioner over the seven provinces of Jing, Xiang, Yi, Ning, Liang, and North and South Qin, made General of Pacifying the West and Governor of Jing Province, while retaining his staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 始興王鑑爲益州，子卿解督。

translations.literal: When Prince of Shixing Xiao Jian became Governor of Yi Province, Ziqing was relieved of the commissionership.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Shixing Xiao Jian took Yi Province, Ziqing was relieved of his supervisory duties.

sentences.zh: 子卿在鎮，營造服飾，多違制度。

translations.literal: When Ziqing was in his province, he made apparel and ornaments, many in violation of regulations.
translations.idiomatic: While Ziqing held his post, he had raiment and ornaments made, many of them in violation of regulations.

sentences.zh: 上勑之曰：「吾前後有勑，非復一兩過，道諸王不得作乖體格服飾，汝何意都不憶吾勑邪？

translations.literal: The Emperor reprimanded him, saying: "I have issued orders before and after, not merely once or twice, stating that princes must not make garments and ornaments of irregular style—why do you not remember my orders at all?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked him: "I have sent order after order—not once or twice—that princes must not commission apparel and ornaments of improper style. Why do you pay no heed to my commands at all?

sentences.zh: 忽作玳瑁乘具，何意？

translations.literal: Suddenly you made tortoiseshell carriage trappings—what is the meaning of this?
translations.idiomatic: You suddenly had tortoiseshell carriage fittings made—what do you mean by this?

sentences.zh: 已成不須壞，可速送下。

translations.literal: Since they are already made, they need not be destroyed; send them down quickly.
translations.idiomatic: They are already finished—no need to destroy them. Send them down to me at once.

sentences.zh: 純銀乘具，乃復可爾，何以作鐙亦是銀？

translations.literal: Pure silver carriage trappings may still be acceptable—why make the stirrups silver as well?
translations.idiomatic: Carriage fittings of pure silver might still pass—but why are the stirrups silver too?

sentences.zh: 可卽壞之。

translations.literal: Destroy them at once.
translations.idiomatic: Break them up immediately.

sentences.zh: 忽用金薄裹箭脚，何意？

translations.literal: Suddenly you used gold leaf to wrap the shaft-end fittings—what is the meaning of this?
translations.idiomatic: You suddenly had the pole-end fittings wrapped in gold leaf—what is this about?

sentences.zh: 亦速壞去。

translations.literal: Destroy them quickly as well.
translations.idiomatic: Get rid of those at once as well.

sentences.zh: 凡諸服章，自今不啓吾知復專輙作者，後有所聞，當復得痛杖。

translations.literal: As to all apparel and insignia, from now on if any are made on your own authority without informing me, whenever I hear of it you shall again receive a severe beating.
translations.idiomatic: For all raiment and regalia: from this day forward, if you again commission anything on your own without telling me, and I hear of it, you will receive a severe flogging.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「汝比在都，讀學不就，年轉成長，吾日冀汝美，勿得勑如風過耳，使吾失氣。」

translations.literal: " He also said: "While you were in the capital, your studies did not succeed; as you grow older year by year, I daily hope you will improve—do not let my orders pass like wind through the ears and make me lose heart."
translations.idiomatic: " He added: "When you were in the capital your studies came to nothing; year by year you grow older, and I look to you daily to improve. Do not let my commands go in one ear and out the other and break my spirit."

sentences.zh: 五年，入爲侍中、撫軍將軍，未拜，仍爲中護軍，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he entered court as Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Army; before he could be invested he was appointed Central Army Commander, retaining Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he entered court as Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Army; before he could take up the post he was made Central Army Commander instead, while retaining Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷秘書監，領右衞將軍，尋遷中軍將軍，侍中竝如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat while holding concurrently General of the Right Guards; soon after he was moved to General of the Central Army, retaining Palace Attendant unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became Director of the Secretariat and concurrently General of the Right Guards; soon after he was promoted to General of the Central Army, with Palace Attendant unchanged.

sentences.zh: 十年，進號車騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year his title was advanced to General of the Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was promoted to General of the Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 俄遷使持節、都督南豫豫司三州軍事、驃騎將軍、南豫州刺史，侍中如故。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over the military affairs of the three provinces South Yu, Yu, and Si, General of the Swift Cavalry, and Governor of South Yu, retaining Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over the military affairs of South Yu, Yu, and Si, made General of the Swift Cavalry and Governor of South Yu, while retaining Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 子卿之鎮，道中戲部伍爲水軍，上聞之，大怒，殺其典籤。

translations.literal: When Ziqing went to his province, on the road he amused himself by drilling his retinue as a naval force; when the Emperor heard of it he was furious and executed Ziqing's registry clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziqing set out for his post he amused himself on the road by drilling his escort as a fleet; the Emperor heard of it, was enraged, and had his registry clerk executed.

sentences.zh: 遣宜都王鏗代之。

translations.literal: He sent Prince of Yidu Xiao Keng to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Prince of Yidu Xiao Keng to take his place.

sentences.zh: 子卿還第，至崩，不與相見。

translations.literal: Ziqing returned to his mansion; until the Emperor's death they did not meet.
translations.idiomatic: Ziqing returned home and, until the Emperor's death, was never received in audience.

sentences.zh: 鬱林卽位，復爲侍中、驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Deposed of Lin took the throne, Ziqing again became Palace Attendant and General of the Swift Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Deposed of Lin ascended the throne, Ziqing was again made Palace Attendant and General of the Swift Cavalry.

sentences.zh: ，轉衞將軍、開府儀同三司，置兵佐。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Guards, Grand Master with golden seal and ceremonials equal to the Three Excellencies, with military staff appointed.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of the Guards and Grand Master with golden seal and ceremonials equal to the Three Excellencies, with military aides assigned.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽王鏘見害，以子卿代爲司徒，領兵置佐。

translations.literal: When Prince of Poyang Xiao Qiang was murdered, Ziqing was appointed in his place as Minister over the Masses, with troops and staff.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince of Poyang Xiao Qiang was killed, Ziqing was appointed Minister over the Masses in his stead, with troops and staff.

sentences.zh: 尋復見殺，時年二十七。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he too was killed; he was twenty-seven years old.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he too was put to death, aged twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 魚復侯子響

translations.literal: Marquis of Yufu Zixiang
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Yufu Zixiang

sentences.zh: 魚復侯子響字雲音，世祖第四子也。

translations.literal: Marquis of Yufu Zixiang, styled name Yunyin, was the fourth son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Yufu Zixiang, courtesy name Yunyin, was the fourth son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 豫章王嶷無子，養子響，後有子，表留爲嫡。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Luan had no sons and adopted Zixiang; later when he had a son of his own, he memorialized to keep Zixiang as his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Luan, being without sons, adopted Zixiang; when he later had a son of his own, he memorialized to retain Zixiang as his heir.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，爲輔國將軍、南彭城臨淮二郡太守，見諸王不致敬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Zixiang was made General Who Supports the State and Administrator of the two commanderies South Pengcheng and Linhuai; he did not pay respects when he saw the other princes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Zixiang was appointed General Who Supports the State and Administrator of South Pengcheng and Linhuai; he refused to bow when he met the other princes.

sentences.zh: 子響勇力絕人，關弓四斛力，數在園池中帖騎馳走竹樹下，身無虧傷。

translations.literal: Zixiang's courage and strength were unmatched; he could draw a bow of four hu strength, and often in the garden ponds would ride brushing through groves of bamboo and trees at full gallop without the slightest injury.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang's valor and strength were beyond compare: he could draw a four-hu bow, and often in the palace gardens would gallop through bamboo groves so close that he brushed the trees, yet never suffered a scratch.

sentences.zh: 旣出繼，車服異諸王，每入朝，輙忿怒，拳打車壁。

translations.literal: After he had been adopted out, his carriage and raiment differed from those of the other princes; each time he entered court he would flare up in anger and pound the carriage wall with his fist.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had been given in adoption, his carriage and dress differed from the other princes'; each time he came to court he would flare up and beat the carriage wall with his fist.

sentences.zh: 世祖知之，令車服與皇子同。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu learned of it, he ordered that Zixiang's carriage and raiment be made the same as those of the imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu learned of this and ordered that his carriage and raiment be made the same as the imperial princes'.

sentences.zh: ，遷右衞將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Right Guards.

sentences.zh: 仍出爲使持節、都督豫州郢州之西陽司州之汝南二郡軍事、冠軍將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was then sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over the military affairs of Xiyang in Yingzhou and Runan in Sizhou, General of the Champions, and Governor of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over the military affairs of Xiyang in Ying Province and Runan in Si Province, General of the Champions, and Governor of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 明年，進號右將軍。

translations.literal: The next year his title was advanced to General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 進督南豫州之歷陽、淮南、潁川、汝陽四郡。

translations.literal: His commission was extended to the four commanderies Liyang, Huainan, Yingchuan, and Ruyang in South Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His supervision was extended to Liyang, Huainan, Yingchuan, and Ruyang in South Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 入爲散騎常侍，右衞將軍。

translations.literal: He entered court as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Right Guards.

sentences.zh: 六年，有司奏：「子響體自聖明，出繼宗國。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the relevant offices memorialized: "Zixiang is in person endowed with sagely brilliance and was adopted out to succeed a collateral state.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the relevant offices memorialized: "Zixiang is in himself endowed with sagely brilliance and was given in adoption to succeed a collateral line.

sentences.zh: 大司馬臣嶷昔未有胤，所以因心鞠養。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal, Minister Luan, in former days had no heir; therefore he nourished and raised Zixiang according to his heart's inclination.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Luan formerly had no heir and therefore raised and nurtured Zixiang as his heart inclined.

sentences.zh: 陛下弘天倫之愛，臣嶷深猶子之恩，遂乃繼體扶疏，世祚垂改，茅蔣菴蔚，冢嗣莫移，誠欣惇睦之風，實虧立嫡之教。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has extended the love of Heaven's kinship; Minister Luan has shown deep affection like unto a son; thus the succession passed to a collateral branch and the hereditary seat would have been altered. Thatch and bamboo grew rank, yet the chief heir was not displaced—a joy at the harmony of kin, but in truth a breach of the teaching to establish the primary heir.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has magnified the bonds of kin; Minister Luan has shown a foster-son's deep affection; thus succession passed to a collateral branch and the hereditary seat nearly changed. Though thatch and bamboo flourished and the chief heir was not displaced, one may rejoice at familial harmony yet in truth this undermines the rule of establishing the primary heir.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，子響宜還本。

translations.literal: We your ministers, having deliberated together, hold that Zixiang ought to return to his original house.
translations.idiomatic: We your ministers, having deliberated, hold that Zixiang ought to return to his birth house.

sentences.zh: 」乃封巴東郡王，遷中護軍，常侍如故。

translations.literal: " He was then enfeoffed as Prince of Badong and transferred to Central Army Commander, retaining Cavalier Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then enfeoffed Prince of Badong and made Central Army Commander, retaining Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 尋出爲江州刺史，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was sent out as Governor of Jiangzhou, retaining Cavalier Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was sent out as Governor of Jiang Province, retaining Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷使持節、都督荊湘雍梁寧南北秦七州軍事、鎮軍將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over the military affairs of the seven provinces Jing, Xiang, Yong, Liang, Ning, and North and South Qin, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over the military affairs of Jing, Xiang, Yong, Liang, Ning, and North and South Qin, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 子響少好武，在西豫時，自選帶仗左右六十人，皆有膽幹。

translations.literal: Zixiang from youth loved the martial arts; while in West Yu he personally selected sixty armed retainers at his side, all men of courage and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zixiang loved the martial arts; while in West Yu he personally chose sixty armed attendants, every one bold and capable.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，數在內齋殺牛置酒，與之聚樂。

translations.literal: On reaching his province, he often slaughtered cattle and set out wine in the inner hall, reveling with them.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he often slaughtered cattle and set out wine in the inner quarters, feasting and making merry with them.

sentences.zh: 令內人私作錦袍絳襖，欲餉蠻交易器仗。

translations.literal: He had palace women secretly make brocade robes and crimson jackets to present to the barbarians in exchange for weapons.
translations.idiomatic: He had palace women secretly make brocade robes and crimson jackets to give the barbarians in exchange for arms.

sentences.zh: 長史劉寅等連名密啓，上勑精檢。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Liu Yin and others jointly submitted a secret memorial under their names; the Emperor ordered a thorough investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Liu Yin and others submitted a joint secret memorial; the Emperor ordered a thorough investigation.

sentences.zh: 寅等懼，欲秘之。

translations.literal: Yin and the others were afraid and wished to keep it secret.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and the others were afraid and wanted to keep the matter concealed.

sentences.zh: 子響聞臺使至，不見勑，召寅及司馬席恭穆、諮議參軍江愈、殷曇粲、中兵參軍周彥、典籤吳脩之、王賢宗、魏景淵於琴臺下詰問之。

translations.literal: When Zixiang heard that capital envoys had arrived but saw no edict, he summoned Yin, Chief Administrator Xi Gongmu, Consultant Jiang Yu, Yin Tan Can, Central Army Staff Officer Zhou Yan, Registry Clerks Wu Xiuzhi, Wang Xianzong, and Wei Jingyuan to the Zither Terrace for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: When Zixiang heard that envoys from the capital had arrived but saw no edict, he summoned Yin, Chief Administrator Xi Gongmu, Consultants Jiang Yu and Yin Tan Can, Central Army Staff Officer Zhou Yan, and Registry Clerks Wu Xiuzhi, Wang Xianzong, and Wei Jingyuan to the Zither Terrace to question them.

sentences.zh: 寅等無言。

translations.literal: Yin and the others said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and the others kept silent.

sentences.zh: 脩之曰：「旣以降勑旨，政應方便答塞。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi said: "Since an edict from above has already come down, we ought for convenience to give evasive answers.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi said: "Since an imperial order has come down, we ought simply to give evasive answers."

sentences.zh: 」景淵曰：「故應先檢校。

translations.literal: " Jingyuan said: "Yet we ought first to conduct the investigation.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingyuan said: "We ought first to carry out the inspection."

sentences.zh: 」子響大怒，執寅等於後堂殺之。

translations.literal: " Zixiang was greatly enraged and seized Yin and the others in the rear hall and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: " Zixiang flew into a rage, seized Yin and the others in the rear hall, and killed them.

sentences.zh: 以啓無江愈名，欲釋之，而用命者已加戮。

translations.literal: Because Jiang Yu's name was not on the memorial he wished to release him, but those who carried out the order had already put him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jiang Yu's name was not on the memorial, Zixiang wished to spare him, but those who carried out the order had already executed him.

sentences.zh: 上聞之怒，遣衞尉胡諧之、游擊將軍尹略、中書舍人茹法亮領齋仗數百人，檢捕羣小。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of it he was furious and sent Commandant of the Guards Hu Xiezhi, General Who Assails in Raid Yin Lue, and Secretariat Gentleman-in-Attendance Ru Faliang, leading several hundred men of the palace guard, to investigate and seize the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard of it he was enraged and sent Commandant of the Guards Hu Xiezhi, General Who Assails in Raid Yin Lue, and Secretariat Gentleman-in-Attendance Ru Faliang, leading several hundred palace guards, to investigate and seize the lesser culprits.

sentences.zh: 勑：「子響若束首自歸，可全其性命。」

translations.literal: An edict stated: "If Zixiang will bind his own head and surrender of himself, his life may be spared."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ran: "If Zixiang will bind his own head and surrender, his life may be spared."

sentences.zh: 諧之等至江津，築城燕尾洲，遣傳詔石伯兒入城慰勞。

translations.literal: When Hu Xiezhi and the others reached the river crossing at Jiangjin, they built a fort on Swallowtail Islet and sent Imperial Messenger Shi Bo'er into the city to offer comfort and labor.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Xiezhi and his party reached the Jiang crossing, built a fort on Swallowtail Islet, and sent Imperial Messenger Shi Bo'er into the city with words of comfort.

sentences.zh: 子響曰：「我不作賊，長史等見負，今政當受殺人罪耳。

translations.literal: Zixiang said: "I am no rebel—the Chief Administrator and the others wronged me; I ought now only to accept punishment for killing men.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang said: "I am no rebel—the Chief Administrator and the others wronged me; I should now accept only the penalty for killing men.

sentences.zh: 」乃殺牛具酒饌，餉臺軍。

translations.literal: " He then slaughtered oxen and set out food and drink to provision the capital troops.
translations.idiomatic: " He then slaughtered oxen, set out food and wine, and sent provisions to the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 而諧之等疑畏，執錄其吏。

translations.literal: Yet Hu Xiezhi and the others, in doubt and fear, seized and bound his clerks.
translations.idiomatic: But Hu Xiezhi and his men, suspicious and afraid, seized and bound his staff.

sentences.zh: 子響怒，遣所養數十人收集府州器仗，令二千人從靈溪西渡，克明旦與臺軍對陣南岸。

translations.literal: Zixiang was enraged and sent several dozen of his household warriors to gather the weapons of the prefectural and provincial government; he ordered two thousand men to cross westward by Spirit Creek, resolving to face the capital army on the south bank at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang was enraged and sent several dozen of his household retainers to gather the prefectural and provincial armory; he ordered two thousand men to cross Spirit Creek by night and meet the imperial army in battle on the south bank at dawn.

sentences.zh: 子響自與百餘人袍騎，將萬鈞弩三四張，宿江堤上。

translations.literal: Zixiang himself, with more than a hundred men in robe and on horseback, took three or four ten-thousand-weight crossbows and encamped on the river embankment.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang himself, with more than a hundred men in white robes on horseback, brought three or four ten-thousand-weight crossbows and camped on the river dike.

sentences.zh: 明日，凶黨與臺軍戰，子響於堤上放弩，亡命王充天等蒙楯陵城，臺軍大敗，尹略死之，官軍引退。

translations.literal: The next day the wicked faction fought the capital army; Zixiang shot crossbows from the embankment; desperate men led by Wang Chongtian and others, shielded, stormed the wall—the capital army suffered a great defeat, Yin Lue died, and the government troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The next day his faction fought the imperial army; Zixiang loosed crossbows from the dike; desperate men led by Wang Chongtian and others, shields raised, stormed the wall—the imperial troops were routed, Yin Lue was killed, and the government army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 上又遣丹陽尹蕭順之領兵繼至，子響部下恐懼，各逃散，子響乃白服降，賜死。

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent Prefect of Danyang Xiao Shunzhi leading troops in succession; Zixiang's followers were afraid and fled each his own way; Zixiang then surrendered in white raiment and was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again sent Prefect of Danyang Xiao Shunzhi with troops in support; Zixiang's followers panicked and scattered; Zixiang then surrendered in white robes and was granted death.

sentences.zh: 時年二十二。

translations.literal: He was twenty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty-two.

sentences.zh: 臨死，啓上曰：「劉寅等入齋檢仗，具如前啓。

translations.literal: On the verge of death he addressed the Emperor: "Liu Yin and the others entered the inner quarters to inspect weapons, exactly as in the earlier memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death he addressed the Emperor: "Liu Yin and the others entered the inner quarters to inspect arms, exactly as in the earlier memorial.

sentences.zh: 臣罪旣山海，分甘斧鉞。

translations.literal: My crime is already mountain and sea in magnitude; I willingly accept axe and ge.
translations.idiomatic: My guilt is already mountain-high and sea-deep; I willingly accept the axe.

sentences.zh: 奉勑遣胡諧之、茹法亮賜重勞，其等至，竟無宣旨，便建旗入津，對城南岸築城守。

translations.literal: By imperial order Hu Xiezhi and Ru Faliang were sent with heavy rewards of favor; when they arrived they announced no edict at all but straightway raised banners and entered the ford, built a fort guarding the south bank opposite the city.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order Hu Xiezhi and Ru Faliang were sent with great tokens of favor; when they arrived they proclaimed no edict at all but straightway raised banners, entered the crossing, and built a fort on the bank opposite the south gate of the city.

sentences.zh: 臣累遣書信喚法亮渡，乞白服相見，其永不肯，羣小懼怖，遂致攻戰，此臣之罪也。

translations.literal: I repeatedly sent letters calling Faliang to cross over, begging to meet him in white raiment; he would never consent—the lesser men were terrified, and thus battle ensued; this is my crime.
translations.idiomatic: I sent letter after letter summoning Faliang to cross the river, begging to meet him in white robes; he would never agree—the lesser men were terrified, and fighting broke out; this is my fault.

sentences.zh: 臣此月二十五日束身投軍，希還天闕，停宅一月，臣自取盡，可使齊代無殺子之譏，臣免逆父之謗。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth of this month I bound myself and submitted to the army, hoping to return to the Heavenly Gate, remain at my mansion one month, and then take my own end—so that the Qi age might not bear the reproach of a slain son and I might escape the slander of unfilial rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth of this month I bound myself and submitted to the army, hoping to return to the capital, stay at my mansion one month, and then take my own life—so that Qi might escape the reproach of killing a son and I might escape the charge of rebelling against my father.

sentences.zh: 旣不遂心，今便命盡，臨啓哽塞，知復何陳。

translations.literal: Since that wish was not granted, I now end my life; as I address this final memorial my throat chokes and I scarce know what more to say.
translations.idiomatic: Since that wish was denied, I now end my life; as I write this final memorial my throat chokes shut and I scarcely know what more to say.

sentences.zh: 」有司奏絕子響屬籍，削爵土，收付廷尉法獄治罪。

translations.literal: " The relevant offices memorialized to strike Zixiang from the genealogical register, strip his fief and rank, and hand him over to the Director of Justice's legal prison for punishment according to law.
translations.idiomatic: " The relevant offices memorialized to strike Zixiang from the genealogical register, strip his fief and rank, and hand him over to the Director of Justice's prison for punishment under law.

sentences.zh: 賜爲蛸氏。

translations.literal: He was given the degrading surname Xiao (蛸, "spider").
translations.idiomatic: He was given the degrading surname Xiao.

sentences.zh: 諸所連坐，別下考論。

translations.literal: All who were implicated in the affair were separately submitted for judgment and review.
translations.idiomatic: All who were implicated were separately submitted for investigation and judgment.

sentences.zh: 贈劉寅侍中，席恭穆輔國將軍、益州刺史，江愈、殷曇粲黃門郎，周彥驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Liu Yin was posthumously awarded Palace Attendant; Xi Gongmu was made General Who Supports the State and Governor of Yi; Jiang Yu and Yin Tan Can were made Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate; Zhou Yan was made General of the Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin was posthumously made Palace Attendant; Xi Gongmu was made General Who Supports the State and Governor of Yi Province; Jiang Yu and Yin Tan Can were made Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate; Zhou Yan was made General of the Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 寅字景蕤，高平人也。

translations.literal: Yin, styled name Jingrao, was a native of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, courtesy name Jingrao, was a man of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 有文義而學不閑世務。

translations.literal: He had mastery of letters and principles but no ease in worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was learned in letters and principles but unskilled in worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 席恭穆，安定焉氏人，關隴豪族。

translations.literal: Xi Gongmu was a man of the Yan clan of Anding, a powerful clan of Guanlong.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Gongmu was of the Yan clan of Anding, a powerful Guanlong family.

sentences.zh: 上憐子響死，後遊華林園，見猿對跳子鳴嘯，上留目久之，因嗚咽流涕。

translations.literal: The Emperor, pitying Zixiang's death, later visited Hualin Garden; when he saw gibbons leaping opposite one another while a young gibbon cried and wailed, he gazed long, then sobbed and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, grieving Zixiang's death, later visited Hualin Garden; when he saw gibbons leaping face to face while a young gibbon cried and wailed, he gazed a long while, then sobbed and wept.

sentences.zh: 豫章王嶷上表曰：「臣聞將而必戮，炳自《春秋》，罄于甸人，著於《經》《禮》，猶懷不忍之言，尚有如倫之痛。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Luan memorialized: "I have heard that he who would be a general must accept execution—this is bright in the Spring and Autumn Annals; executing criminals in the suburbs is set forth in the Classics and Rites; yet even so one cherishes words of unwillingness, and still feels pain like unto suffering kin.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Luan memorialized: "I have heard that a commander who fails must face execution—this shines forth in the Spring and Autumn Annals; putting criminals to death in the suburbs is recorded in the Classics and Rites; yet even so one still cherishes words of unwillingness and still feels the pain of kinship.

sentences.zh: 豈不事因法往，情以恩留。

translations.literal: Surely affairs follow where the law leads, while affection remains where grace touches.
translations.idiomatic: Surely affairs follow the law, while feeling lingers where grace has touched.

sentences.zh: 故庶人蛸子響，識懷靡樹，見淪不逞，肆憤一朝，取陷凶德，遂使迹隣非孝，事近無君，身膏草野，未云塞釁。

translations.literal: Thus the commoner of the Xiao clan, Zixiang, whose understanding could find no foothold and who, seeing himself wronged, could not restrain his impulse, in a single morning poured forth his wrath and fell into wicked conduct, so that his traces bordered on unfiliality and his deeds approached rebellion; his body greased the wild grass, and the offense was scarcely expiated.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the commoner Zixiang of the Xiao clan, whose mind found no footing and who, seeing himself wronged, could not restrain himself, in a single morning poured out his rage and fell into wicked conduct, so that his conduct bordered on unfiliality and his deeds approached treason; his body greased the wild grass, and the offense was scarcely atoned.

sentences.zh: 但韔矢倒戈，歸罪司戮，卽理原心，亦旣迷而知返。

translations.literal: Yet he cast aside his bow and turned his blades, returning guilt to the punisher; when one searches out the mind in principle, he had already lost his way and yet knew to return.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he cast aside his bowcase and turned his blades, returning guilt to the executioner; judged by principle and searched to the heart, he had lost his way yet knew to turn back.

sentences.zh: 釁骨不收，辜魂莫赦，撫事惟往，載傷心目。

translations.literal: His guilty bones were not gathered in, his wronged soul received no pardon; contemplating the past I can only grieve, for it wounds the eye of the heart.
translations.idiomatic: His guilty bones were not gathered in, his wronged soul received no pardon; as I look back on what passed, it wounds the eye of the heart.

sentences.zh: 昔閔榮伏○，愴動墳園；

translations.literal: Of old Min Rong fell on his sword [lacuna: ○, likely 劍], moving the burial ground to grief;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Min Rong fell on his sword [text damaged: ○], stirring grief at the ancestral graves;

sentences.zh: 思荊就辟，側懷丘墓。

translations.literal: Jing Ke, bound for his commission, felt tenderly for the mound and tomb at home.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Ke, bound for his mission, felt tenderly for the graves at home.

sentences.zh: 皆兩臣釁結於明時，二主議加於盛世，積代用之爲美，歷史不以云非。

translations.literal: Both were ministers whose offenses were knit in an enlightened age, and both lords deliberated addition of grace in a flourishing era—successive ages have taken this as beautiful, and histories do not regard it as wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Both were ministers whose offenses were sealed in an enlightened age, and both sovereigns deliberated added grace in a flourishing era—successive ages have taken this as admirable, and histories do not call it wrong.

sentences.zh: 伏願一下天矝，爰詔蛸氏，使得安兆末郊，旋窆餘麓，微列葦輤之容，薄申封樹之禮。

translations.literal: I venture to beg that Heaven's grace descend, and that an edict issue to the Xiao clan, so that he may be settled at the edge of the tomb precinct and turned to burial in what remains of the hills, with slight display of rush-carriage show and thin observance of the rites of enfeoffment and planting.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to beg that Heaven's grace descend and an edict issue to the Xiao clan, so that he may be laid at the edge of the tomb precinct and buried in what remains of the hills, with slight display of rush-carriage ceremony and modest observance of the rites of planting the grave mound.

sentences.zh: 豈伊窮骸被德，實且天下歸仁。

translations.literal: Could this be only that his impoverished bones receive virtue? In truth the world would return to humanity.
translations.idiomatic: Would this be only that his poor bones receive grace? In truth the realm would return to humanity.

sentences.zh: 臣屬忝皇枝，偏留友睦，以臣繼別未安，子響言承出命，提攜鞠養，俯見成人，雖輟胤蕃條，歸體琁萼，循執之念不移，傅訓之憐何已。

translations.literal: I, your minister, share in the imperial branch yet bear a special bond of friendship and harmony; because I adopted him to another house I was not at ease, yet Zixiang spoke of carrying out the command to leave; I raised and nourished him, looking down to see him grown to manhood—though I yielded an heir on the collateral branch and he returned to the pearl calyx of the imperial line, the thought I hold in my hand does not shift, nor the pity of the foster father's instruction ever end.
translations.idiomatic: I, your minister, share in the imperial branch yet bear a special bond of friendship; because I gave him in adoption I was uneasy, yet Zixiang spoke of carrying out the command to leave; I raised and nurtured him and watched him grow to manhood—though I yielded an heir on the collateral branch and he returned to the imperial stem, the hand I hold does not loosen, nor the foster father's pity ever end.

sentences.zh: 敢冒宸嚴，布此悲乞。

translations.literal: I dare trespass on the august majesty to lay forth this grief-stricken plea.
translations.idiomatic: I dare trespass on the august majesty to lay forth this grief-stricken plea.

sentences.zh: 」上不許。

translations.literal: " The Emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor did not grant it.

sentences.zh: 先是貶爲魚復侯。

translations.literal: Earlier he had been degraded to Marquis of Yufu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had been demoted to Marquis of Yufu.

sentences.zh: 安陸王子敬

translations.literal: Prince of Anlu Zijing
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Anlu Zijing

sentences.zh: 安陸王子敬字雲端，世祖第五子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Anlu Zijing, styled name Yunduan, was the fifth son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Anlu Zijing, courtesy name Yunduan, was the fifth son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 初封應城縣公。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was enfeoffed Duke of Yingcheng.

sentences.zh: ，出爲持節、監南兖兖徐青冀五州、北中郎將、南兖州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of the five provinces South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General of the North Central Army, and Governor of South Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General of the North Central Army, and Governor of South Yan.

sentences.zh: 四年，進號右軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year his title was advanced to General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 明年，徙都督荊湘梁雍南北秦六州軍事、平西將軍、荊州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Commissioner over the military affairs of the six provinces Jing, Xiang, Liang, Yong, and North and South Qin, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Jing, retaining Bearer of the Staff as before.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Commissioner over the military affairs of Jing, Xiang, Liang, Yong, and North and South Qin, made General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Jing Province, while retaining his staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 尋進號安西將軍。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 七年，徵侍中，護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was summoned as Palace Attendant and General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was summoned to court as Palace Attendant and General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 十年，轉散騎常侍、撫軍將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Prefect of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he became Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Prefect of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 十一年，進車騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was advanced to General of the Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to General of the Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尋給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was granted one suite of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was granted one suite of martial pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: ，遷使持節、都督南兖兖徐青冀五州、征北大將軍、南兖州刺史。

translations.literal: , he was transferred as Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over the five provinces South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, Grand General Who Campaigns North, and Governor of South Yan.
translations.idiomatic: , he was transferred as Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, made Grand General Who Campaigns North and Governor of South Yan.

sentences.zh: ，加侍中。

translations.literal: , and was additionally appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: , and was additionally appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 高宗除諸蕃王，遣中護軍王玄邈

translations.literal: Emperor Ming removed the various feudatory princes and sent Central Guardian General Wang Xuanyao
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming purged the feudatory princes, he sent Central Guardian General Wang Xuanyao

sentences.zh: 〈征九江〉

translations.literal: 〈Campaign against Jiujiang〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Campaign against Jiujiang〉

sentences.zh: ，王廣之襲殺子敬，時年二十三。

translations.literal: ; Wang Guangzhi attacked and killed Zijing. He was twenty-three years of age.
translations.idiomatic: ; Wang Guangzhi attacked and killed Zijing. He was twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 晉安王子懋

translations.literal: Prince of Jin'an Zimao
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin'an Zimao

sentences.zh: 晉安王子懋字雲昌，世祖第七子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin'an Zimao, courtesy name Yunchang, was the seventh son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin'an Zimao, courtesy name Yunchang, was the seventh son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 初封江陵公。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed Duke of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was enfeoffed Duke of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: ，爲持節、都督南豫豫司三州、南中郎將、南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: , appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over the three provinces South Yu, Yu, and Si, General of the South Central Army, and Governor of South Yu.
translations.idiomatic: , he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over South Yu, Yu, and Si, General of the South Central Army, and Governor of South Yu.

sentences.zh: 魚復侯子響爲豫州，子懋解督。

translations.literal: When the Marquis of Yufu Zixiang became Governor of Yu, Zimao relinquished his commissionership.
translations.idiomatic: When the Marquis of Yufu Zixiang took charge of Yu Province, Zimao gave up his supervisory role.

sentences.zh: 四年，進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year his title was advanced to General Who Campaigns Abroad.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to General Who Campaigns Abroad.

sentences.zh: 南豫新置，力役寡少，加子懋領宣城太守。

translations.literal: South Yu had been newly established and corvée labor was scant; Zimao was additionally made Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Because South Yu had only recently been established and labor levies were few, Zimao was also appointed Administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 明年，爲監南兖兖徐青冀五州軍事、後將軍、南兖州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: The next year he was made Supervisor of military affairs in the five provinces South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, Rear General, and Governor of South Yan, retaining Bearer of the Staff as before.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became Supervisor of military affairs in South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, Rear General, and Governor of South Yan, while retaining his staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 六年，徙監湘州、平南將軍、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Supervisor of Xiang Province, General Who Pacifies the South, and Governor of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to Supervisor of Xiang Province, made General Who Pacifies the South, and appointed Governor of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 明年，加持節、都督。

translations.literal: The next year Bearer of the Staff and Commissioner were added.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was given Bearer of the Staff and made Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 八年，進號鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year his title was advanced to General Who Guards the South.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to General Who Guards the South.

sentences.zh: 撰《春秋例苑》三十卷奏之，世祖嘉之，勑付秘閣。

translations.literal: He compiled Exemplary Cases from the Spring and Autumn Annals in thirty scrolls and presented it; Emperor Wu commended it and ordered it deposited in the secret archives.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Exemplary Cases from the Spring and Autumn Annals in thirty scrolls and presented it to the throne; Emperor Wu praised the work and ordered it placed in the imperial archives.

sentences.zh: 九年，親府州事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he personally attended to prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he personally managed the affairs of his commandery.

sentences.zh: 十年，入爲侍中，領右衞將軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he entered court as Palace Attendant and concurrently General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he came to court as Palace Attendant and concurrently commanded the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷散騎常侍，中書監。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he became Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 未拜，仍爲使持節、都督雍梁南北秦四州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡軍事、征北將軍、雍州刺史，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Before he could assume the post, he was again made Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over military affairs in the four provinces Yong, Liang, and North and South Qin, Jingling in Jing Province, and Suizhou in Si Province, General Who Campaigns North, and Governor of Yong, and was granted one suite of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up the appointment, he was again made Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, Jingling in Jing Province, and Suizhou in Si Province, General Who Campaigns North, and Governor of Yong, with one suite of martial pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 豫章王喪服未畢，上以邊州須威望，許得奏之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang was still in mourning; because the frontier province required prestige, the emperor allowed him to report for duty.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang had not yet completed mourning, but because the border province needed his prestige, the emperor permitted him to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 鬱林卽位，卽本號爲大將軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yulin ascended the throne, Zimao was promoted on his existing title to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yulin took the throne, Zimao was advanced from his current rank to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 子懋見幼主新立，密懷自全之計。

translations.literal: Seeing the young sovereign newly enthroned, Zimao secretly devised plans to preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the young emperor newly installed, Zimao secretly laid plans for his own safety.

sentences.zh: 令作部造器仗。

translations.literal: He ordered workshops to manufacture weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: He had workshops forge weapons and armor.

sentences.zh: 陳顯達時爲征虜，屯襄陽，欲脅取以爲將帥。

translations.literal: Chen Xianda was then General Who Campaigns Abroad, stationed at Xiangyang, and wished to coerce him into serving as his commander.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda, then General Who Campaigns Abroad, was encamped at Xiangyang and meant to force him into becoming his field commander.

sentences.zh: 顯達密啓，高宗徵顯達還。

translations.literal: Xianda sent a secret memorial, and Emperor Ming summoned Xianda back.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda reported in secret, and Emperor Ming recalled him to court.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，遷子懋爲都督江州刺史，留西楚部曲助鎮襄陽，單將白直俠轂自隨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang, Zimao was transferred to Commissioner of Jiang Province; the Western Chu troops were left to help garrison Xiangyang, while he went alone with a band of white-clad daredevils in his train.
translations.idiomatic: In Longchang year 1, Zimao was moved to Commissioner of Jiang Province; he left his Western Chu detachments to help hold Xiangyang and went forth alone with a train of white-clad bravos.

sentences.zh: 顯達入別，子懋謂曰：「朝廷令身單身而反，身是天王，豈可過爾輕率。

translations.literal: When Xianda came in to take leave, Zimao said to him: "The court orders me to return alone. I am a Son of Heaven—how could I be so reckless.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda came in to bid farewell, and Zimao said, "The court commands me to return by myself. I am a prince of the blood—how can I be so careless.

sentences.zh: 今猶欲將二三千人自隨，公意何如？

translations.literal: Even now I still wish to take two or three thousand men with me—what do you think, sir?"
translations.idiomatic: I still want to bring two or three thousand men along. What is your view, sir?"

sentences.zh: 」顯達曰：「殿下若不留部曲，便是大違勑旨，其事不輕。

translations.literal: " Xianda said: "If Your Highness does not leave your troops behind, you will gravely violate the imperial order—a matter of no small weight.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda replied, "If Your Highness keeps your troops, you will seriously defy the imperial command. The matter is grave.

sentences.zh: 且此閒人亦難可收用。

translations.literal: Besides, the men here are hard to employ in any case."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, these men here are scarcely fit to be used."

sentences.zh: 」子懋默然，顯達因辭出便發去，子懋計未立，還鎮尋陽。

translations.literal: " Zimao fell silent. Xianda took his leave and set off at once; Zimao's plans were not yet settled, and he returned to garrison Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zimao said nothing. Xianda withdrew and departed immediately; Zimao's scheme was not yet ready, and he went back to hold Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he was additionally appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxing year 1 he was additionally made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 聞鄱陽隨郡二王見殺，欲起兵赴難。

translations.literal: On hearing that the Princes of Poyang and Suizhou had been killed, he wished to raise troops to rush to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that the Princes of Poyang and Suizhou had been slain, he meant to raise an army to go to their rescue.

sentences.zh: 母阮在都，遣書欲密迎上，阮報其兄于瑤之爲計，瑤之馳告高宗。

translations.literal: His mother Ruan was in the capital; he sent a letter wishing to bring her up in secret. Ruan informed her elder brother Yu Yaozhi to devise a plan, and Yaozhi galloped to report to Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Ruan was in the capital; he wrote wishing to bring her up secretly. She told her elder brother Yu Yaozhi to work out a plan, and Yaozhi rode posthaste to inform Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 於是纂嚴，遣平西將軍王廣之南北討，使軍主裴叔業與瑤之先襲尋陽，聲云爲郢州行司馬。

translations.literal: Thereupon strict orders were issued; Grand General Who Pacifies the West Wang Guangzhi was sent on a punitive expedition north and south, and the army commander Pei Shuye with Yaozhi were first to strike Xunyang, claiming to be acting prefect of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Orders were tightened at once; Wang Guangzhi, General Who Pacifies the West, was dispatched on a campaign north and south, while the army commander Pei Shuye and Yaozhi were sent ahead to surprise Xunyang, announcing that they were the acting prefect of Ying.

sentences.zh: 子懋知之，遣三百人守盆城。

translations.literal: When Zimao learned of it, he sent three hundred men to hold Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this, Zimao sent three hundred men to defend Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 叔業泝流直上，至夜回下襲盆城。

translations.literal: Shuye went upriver and, at night, turned downstream to strike Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye sailed upstream, then at night turned back downstream to assault Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 城局參軍樂賁開門納之。

translations.literal: Yue Ben, a staff officer of the city bureau, opened the gate and admitted him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Ben, a staff officer in the city bureau, opened the gates and let him in.

sentences.zh: 子懋率府州兵力，先已具船於稽亭渚，聞叔業得盆城，乃據州自衞。

translations.literal: Zimao led the military strength of the prefecture and commandery; boats had already been prepared at Jiting Ford. When he heard that Shuye had taken Pencheng, he then held the province to defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zimao mustered the forces of his prefecture and province; boats had already been readied at Jiting Ford. Hearing that Shuye had seized Pencheng, he barricaded himself in the provincial seat.

sentences.zh: 子懋部曲多雍土人，皆踊躍願奮，叔業畏之，遣于瑤之說子懋曰：「今還都，必無過憂，政當作散官，不失富貴也。

translations.literal: Many of Zimao's followers were natives of Yong; all leapt up eager to fight. Shuye feared them and sent Yu Yaozhi to persuade Zimao, saying: "If you return to the capital now, you will certainly have no cause for anxiety; you will merely be made an honorary official and will not lose wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Zimao's troops were men of Yong, and they all sprang up willing to fight. Shuye was afraid of them and sent Yu Yaozhi to tell Zimao, "Return to the capital now and you will surely have nothing to fear; you will only be given an honorary post and will not lose your fortune and standing.

sentences.zh: 」子懋旣不出兵攻叔業，衆情稍沮。

translations.literal: " Since Zimao would not send troops to attack Shuye, the men's ardor gradually waned.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zimao would not march out against Shuye, the troops' spirit slowly faded.

sentences.zh: 中兵參軍于琳之，瑤之兄也。

translations.literal: Central Army Major Yu Linzhi was Yaozhi's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Linzhi, Central Army Major, was Yaozhi's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 說子懋重賂叔業，子懋使琳之往。

translations.literal: He urged Zimao to bribe Shuye heavily, and Zimao sent Linzhi to him.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded Zimao to offer Shuye a heavy bribe, and Zimao dispatched Linzhi.

sentences.zh: 琳之因說叔業請取子懋，叔業遣軍主徐玄慶將四百人隨琳之入州城，僚佐皆奔散，琳之從二百人拔白入齋，子懋罵曰：「小人何忍行此事。

translations.literal: Linzhi then urged Shuye to seize Zimao. Shuye sent the army commander Xu Xuanqing with four hundred men to follow Linzhi into the provincial city; the staff all fled and scattered. Linzhi led two hundred men, swords drawn, into the private quarters. Zimao cursed him: "How could a petty man bear to do such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Linzhi then persuaded Shuye to take Zimao captive. Shuye sent the army commander Xu Xuanqing with four hundred men to enter the provincial city with Linzhi; the officials all fled. Linzhi entered the residence with two hundred men, blades bare. Zimao railed at him: "How can a base fellow endure to do this.

sentences.zh: 」琳之以袖鄣面，使人害之。

translations.literal: " Linzhi covered his face with his sleeve and had men kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Linzhi hid his face in his sleeve and had him slain.

sentences.zh: 時年二十三。

translations.literal: He was twenty-three years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 初，子懋鎮雍，世祖勑以邊略曰：「吾比連得諸處啓，所說不異，虜必無敢送死理，然爲其備，不可蹔懈。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zimao was stationed in Yong, Emperor Wu instructed him on frontier strategy, saying: "I have lately received one report after another from every quarter, all saying the same thing: the barbarians surely have no mind to come and die here—yet make ready against them; do not relax even for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Zimao held Yong, Emperor Wu wrote him on frontier strategy: "Reports have been arriving in steady succession from every post, all alike: the northerners surely will not come seeking death—yet prepare against them and do not slacken for an instant.

sentences.zh: 今秋犬羊輩越逸者，其亡滅之徵。

translations.literal: Those dog-and-goat bands that slip the leash this autumn are the sign of their coming ruin.
translations.idiomatic: When the dog-and-goat rabble break loose this autumn, it will be the omen of their destruction.

sentences.zh: 吾今亦行密纂集，須有分明指的，便當有大處分。

translations.literal: I too am now conducting a secret muster; once there is a clear target, there will at once be a major disposition.
translations.idiomatic: I am mustering in secret as well; once we have a definite aim, I shall act on a large scale at once.

sentences.zh: 今普勑鎮守，竝部偶民丁，有事卽便應接運，已勑更遣，想行有至者，汝共諸人量覔，可使人數往南陽舞陰諸要處參覘。

translations.literal: I now broadly order every garrison to draft corvée men in pairs; if anything happens, transport and relief are to be provided at once. I have already ordered further detachments—some should be arriving on the road. You and the others should gauge the situation and send men south to the key points at Nanyang and Wuyin to reconnoiter.
translations.idiomatic: I have now ordered all frontier commands to levy corvée laborers in pairs; if trouble arises, supply and transport must respond immediately. More troops are already on the way. You and your staff should judge the situation and send men to the critical points at Nanyang and Wuyin to observe.

sentences.zh: 糧食最爲根本，更不憂人仗，常行視驛亭馬，不可有廢闕。

translations.literal: Grain is the root of all else; do not worry over manpower and arms. Inspect the relay horses regularly—there must be no lapse.
translations.idiomatic: Grain is the foundation; arms are secondary. Keep checking the post-station horses and let none fall idle.

sentences.zh: 并約語諸州，當其堺皆爾，不如法，卽問事。

translations.literal: Also instruct every province that all along the borders it must be the same; whoever falls short of the rule will be called to account."
translations.idiomatic: Tell every province as well that the border districts must all follow this rule; whoever fails will answer for it."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「吾勑荊、郢二鎮，各作五千人陣，本擬應接彼耳。

translations.literal: " He also said: "I have ordered the two commands of Jing and Ying each to form arrays of five thousand men, originally intended to support that front.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "I have ordered the Jing and Ying commands each to form formations of five thousand men, meant to reinforce that theater.

sentences.zh: 賊若送死者，更卽呼取之。

translations.literal: If the enemy comes to die, summon them at once.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy actually comes to fight, call them up immediately.

sentences.zh: 已勑子真，魚繼宗、殷公愍至鎮，可以公愍爲城主，三千人配之便足。

translations.literal: I have already ordered Zizhen; Yu Jizong and Yin Gongmin will reach the command—Gongmin may serve as city commander, and three thousand men assigned to him will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: I have instructed Zizhen; Yu Jizong and Yin Gongmin will reach your post. Make Gongmin city commander—three thousand men allotted to him are enough.

sentences.zh: 汝可好以階級在意，勿得人求，或超五三階。

translations.literal: You must keep rank and grade firmly in mind; do not grant favors on petition, or leap five or three grades at a stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Watch rank and grade carefully; do not promote men on request by five or three steps at once.

sentences.zh: 及文章詩筆，乃是佳事，然世務彌爲根本，可常憶之。

translations.literal: Literary composition, poetry, and brushwork are fine things, yet public affairs are ever more fundamental—keep that always in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Essays, verse, and the brush are worthy pursuits, but state business is the root—remember that constantly.

sentences.zh: 汝所啓仗，此悉是吾左右御仗也，云何得用之。

translations.literal: The arms you requested in your memorial are all my personal guard weapons—how could you use them?"
translations.idiomatic: The weapons you asked for are all from my own guard—how could you take them?"

sentences.zh: 品格不可乖，吾自當優量覔送。

translations.literal: Grades must not be bent; I myself will see that suitable ones are sent in generous measure."
translations.idiomatic: Do not bend the standards of quality; I shall personally choose and send what is fitting."

sentences.zh: 」先是啓求所好書，上又曰：「知汝常以書讀在心，足爲深欣也。

translations.literal: " Earlier he had memorialized requesting books he favored, and the emperor also said: "Knowing that you always keep reading in your heart fills me with deep pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had asked for favorite books, and the emperor also wrote, "Knowing you keep study close to your heart gives me great joy.

sentences.zh: 」賜子懋杜預手所定《左傳》及《古今善言》。

translations.literal: " He granted Zimao Du Yu's hand-edited Zuo Tradition and Good Words Ancient and Modern.
translations.idiomatic: He bestowed on Zimao Du Yu's own recension of the Zuo Tradition and Good Words Ancient and Modern.

sentences.zh: 隨郡王子隆

translations.literal: Prince of Suizhou Zilong
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Suizhou Zilong

sentences.zh: 隨郡王子隆字雲興，世祖第八子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Suizhou Zilong, courtesy name Yunxing, was the eighth son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Suizhou Zilong, courtesy name Yunxing, was the eighth son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 有文才。

translations.literal: He had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed literary talent.

sentences.zh: 初封枝江公。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed Duke of Zhijiang.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was enfeoffed Duke of Zhijiang.

sentences.zh: ，爲輔國將軍、南琅邪彭城二郡太守。

translations.literal: , made General Who Supports the State and Administrator of the two commanderies South Langye and Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: , he was made General Who Supports the State and Administrator of South Langye and Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷江州刺史，未拜，唐宇之賊平，遷爲持節、督會稽東陽新安臨海永嘉五郡、東中郎將、會稽太守。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Governor of Jiang; before he could assume the post, the bandit Tang Yuzhi was pacified, and he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over the five commanderies Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, and Yongjia, General of the East Central Army, and Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was moved to Jiang Province; before taking office, the outlaw Tang Yuzhi was suppressed, and he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, and Yongjia, General of the East Central Army, and Administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 遷長兼中書令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to act concurrently as Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to serve concurrently as Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 子隆娶尚書令王儉女爲妃，上以子隆能屬文，謂儉曰：「我家東阿也。
