translations.literal: Zilong married the daughter of Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian as his consort. Because Zilong could compose literary pieces, the emperor said to Jian: "In our house, Dong'e has returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zilong took as consort the daughter of Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian. The emperor, noting Zilong's literary skill, told Jian, "We have another Dong'e in the family.

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「東阿重出，實爲皇家蕃屏。

translations.literal: " Jian said: "Dong'e reborn—truly a bulwark of the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: Jian replied, "Dong'e born again—indeed a screen for the royal house.

sentences.zh: 」未及拜，仍遷中護軍，轉侍中、左衞將軍。

translations.literal: " Before he could assume the post, he was transferred to Central Guardian General, then to Palace Attendant and General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up the appointment, he became Central Guardian General, then Palace Attendant and General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 八年，代魚復侯子響爲使持節、都督荊雍梁寧南北秦六州、鎮西將軍、荊州刺史，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he replaced the Marquis of Yufu Zixiang as Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over the six provinces Jing, Yong, Liang, Ning, and North and South Qin, General Who Guards the West, and Governor of Jing, and was granted one suite of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he succeeded the Marquis of Yufu Zixiang as Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over Jing, Yong, Liang, Ning, and North and South Qin, General Who Guards the West, and Governor of Jing, with one suite of martial pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 其年，始興王鑑罷益州，進號督益州。

translations.literal: That year the Prince of Shixing relinquished Yi Province, and his title was advanced to Commissioner of Yi as well.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the Prince of Shixing gave up Yi Province, and he was further made Commissioner of Yi.

sentences.zh: 九年，親府州事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he personally attended to prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he personally managed the affairs of his commandery.

sentences.zh: 十一年，晉安王子懋爲雍州，子隆復解督。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Prince of Jin'an Zimao took Yong Province, and Zilong again relinquished his commissionership.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when Prince of Jin'an Zimao received Yong Province, Zilong again gave up his supervisory role.

sentences.zh: 鬱林立，進號征西將軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yulin ascended the throne, his title was advanced to General Who Campaigns West.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yulin took the throne, he was promoted to General Who Campaigns West.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，爲侍中、撫軍將軍，領兵置佐。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he was made Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Army, with military staff appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In Longchang year 1 he became Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Army, with troops and aides assigned.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，轉中軍大將軍，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he was transferred to Grand General of the Central Army, retaining Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxing year 1 he was moved to Grand General of the Central Army while remaining Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 子隆年二十一，而體過充壯，常服蘆茹丸以自銷損。

translations.literal: Zilong was twenty-one, yet his frame was overly robust; he regularly took rush-root pills to reduce himself.
translations.idiomatic: Though only twenty-one, Zilong was excessively stout; he often swallowed rush-root pills to slim himself.

sentences.zh: 高宗輔政，謀害諸王，世祖諸子中，子隆最以才貌見憚，故與鄱陽王鏘同夜先見殺。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming held the regency and plotted to destroy the princes, among Emperor Wu's sons Zilong was most feared for talent and looks; therefore he and the Prince of Poyang were killed the same night, ahead of the others.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, as regent, schemed against the princes; of Emperor Wu's sons, Zilong was most dreaded for ability and appearance, and so he and the Prince of Poyang were slain the same night before the rest.

sentences.zh: 文集行於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His literary collection circulated publicly.

sentences.zh: 建安王子真

translations.literal: Prince of Jian'an Zizhen
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jian'an Zizhen

sentences.zh: 建安王子真字雲仙，世祖第九子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Jian'an Zizhen, courtesy name Yunxian, was the ninth son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jian'an Zizhen, courtesy name Yunxian, was the ninth son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: ，爲輔國將軍、南琅邪彭城二郡太守。

translations.literal: , made General Who Supports the State and Administrator of the two commanderies South Langye and Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: , he was made General Who Supports the State and Administrator of South Langye and Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 遷持節、督南豫司二州軍事、冠軍將軍、南豫州刺史，領宣城太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over military affairs in the two provinces South Yu and Si, General Who Champions, and Governor of South Yu, concurrently Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over South Yu and Si, General Who Champions, and Governor of South Yu, while also holding Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 進號南中郎將。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to General of the South Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the South Central Army.

sentences.zh: 六年，以府州稍實，表解領郡。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, because the prefectural establishment had grown somewhat substantial, he memorialized to relinquish his concurrent commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, as his provincial staff had become somewhat full, he asked to give up the concurrent prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七年，進號右將軍，遷丹陽尹，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the seventh year his title was advanced to General of the Right; he was transferred to Prefect of Danyang, retaining his generalship as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to General of the Right and made Prefect of Danyang, keeping his military title.

sentences.zh: 轉左衞將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to General of the Left Guard.

translations.literal: (seventh)
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year

sentences.zh: 年，遷中護軍，仍出爲持節、都督郢司二州軍事、平西將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: year, he was transferred to Central Guardian General; he then went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over military affairs in the two provinces Ying and Si, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: , he was transferred to Central Guardian General, then went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over Ying and Si, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Ying.

sentences.zh: 鬱林立，進號安西將軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yulin ascended the throne, his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yulin took the throne, he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，爲散騎常侍、護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he was made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Longchang year 1 he became Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，轉鎮軍將軍，領兵置佐，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he was transferred to General Who Guards the Army, with military staff appointed, retaining Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxing year 1 he was moved to General Who Guards the Army with troops and aides assigned, while remaining Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 其年見殺，年十九。

translations.literal: That year he was killed. He was nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was slain. He was nineteen.

sentences.zh: 西陽王子明

translations.literal: Prince of Xiyang Ziming
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiyang Ziming

sentences.zh: 西陽王子明字雲光，世祖第十子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiyang Ziming, courtesy name Yunguang, was the tenth son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiyang Ziming, courtesy name Yunguang, was the tenth son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: ，封武昌王。

translations.literal: , enfeoffed Prince of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: , he was enfeoffed Prince of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 三年，失國璽，改封西陽。

translations.literal: In the third year he lost the state seal of the realm and was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he lost the imperial state seal and was re-enfeoffed Prince of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 六年，爲持節、都督南兖兖徐青冀五州軍事、冠軍將軍、南兖州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over military affairs in the five provinces Southern Yanzhou, Yanzhou, Xuzhou, Qingzhou, and Jizhou, General Who Champions, and Governor of Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became Bearer of the Staff, Commissioner over Southern Yanzhou, Yanzhou, Xuzhou, Qingzhou, and Jizhou, General Who Champions, and Governor of Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year his title was advanced to General Who Punishes the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to General Who Punishes the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 十年，進左將軍，仍爲督會稽東陽臨海永嘉新安五郡軍事、會稽太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to General of the Left and concurrently made Commissioner over military affairs in the five commanderies Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, and Xin'an, and Administrator of Kuaiji, retaining his generalship as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was promoted to General of the Left and made Commissioner over Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, and Xin'an, with the post of Administrator of Kuaiji, keeping his military title.

sentences.zh: 子明風姿明淨，士女觀者，咸嗟嘆之。

translations.literal: Ziming's bearing was bright and pure; men and women who saw him all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Ziming's bearing was bright and pure; men and women who glimpsed him all sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 鬱林初，進號平東將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Prince of Yulin's reign, his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yulin first took the throne, he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，爲右將軍、中書令。

translations.literal: In Longchang year 1 he was made General of the Right and Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: In Longchang year 1 he became General of the Right and Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，遷侍中，領驍騎將軍，右軍如故。

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：民之勞逸，隨所遭遇，習以成性，有識斯同。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Whether the people toil or rest follows what they encounter; habit becomes character, and the perceptive agree on this.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Whether people labor or rest follows what they meet; habit becomes nature, and the clear-sighted agree.

sentences.zh: 帝王子弟，生長尊貴，薪禽之道未知，富厚之圖已極。

translations.literal: Imperial princes and sons grow up in exalted privilege; they know nothing of gathering fuel and catching birds, yet the prospect of wealth is already at its limit.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of emperors and kings are reared in exalted rank; they do not know the ways of fuel and fowl, yet the map of riches is already at its end.

sentences.zh: 齠年稚齒，養器深宮，習趨拜之儀，受文句之學，坐躡搢紳，傍絕交友，情偽之事，不經耳目，憂懼之道，未涉胷衿，雖卓爾天悟，自得懷抱，孤寡爲識，所陋猶多。

translations.literal: From tender years they are bred in the deep palace, drilled in court obeisance, taught phrases from the classics, seated among silk-clad officials with no friends at their side; the affairs of truth and falsehood never reach their eyes and ears, the ways of worry and fear never touch their breast. Though by nature exceptionally quick, they cherish their own conceits; isolated in judgment, they lack much.
translations.idiomatic: In childhood they are raised in the deep palace, trained in bowing and yielding, taught lines from the classics, seated among gentry with no friends near them; the business of truth and sham never passes their eyes and ears, the road of worry and dread never enters their breast. Though exceptionally gifted by Heaven and sure of their own minds, their knowledge is solitary — how much they still lack.

sentences.zh: 朝出閫閨，暮司方岳，帝子臨州，親民尚小，年序次第，宜屏皇家，防驕剪逸，積代恒典，平允之情，操捶貽慮。

translations.literal: They leave the inner gate in the morning and by evening govern a province; an imperial son takes up a prefecture when the people he is to cherish are still small; by rank and age he ought to stand apart from the ruling house — curbing pride, trimming excess — a constant practice of former ages, the equitable concern that the rod may be passed down.
translations.idiomatic: They leave the inner quarters at dawn and by dusk command a province; an imperial son governs a region while the people are still young; by age and order he should stand apart from the royal house — guarding against pride, cutting off license — the constant rule of former ages, the fair fear that the rod may be handed on.

sentences.zh: 故輔以上佐，簡自帝心，勞舊左右，用爲主帥，州國府第，先令後行，飲食遊居，動應聞啓，端拱守祿，遵承法度，張弛之要，莫敢厝言，行事執其權，典籤掣其肘，苟利之義未申，專違之咎已及。

translations.literal: Hence they are assisted by high deputies chosen from the emperor's own men, veteran attendants made commanders; in the prefecture or princely residence orders go out before deeds follow, in eating and roaming every move is reported; they sit upright guarding their stipend and obey the law — none dares speak on tightening or loosening restraint; the chief aide holds power, the registry clerk pulls their elbow; where profit is slight, the fault for going alone is already at hand.
translations.idiomatic: So they are aided by senior assistants chosen from the emperor's heart, old retainers at the left and right made commanders; in the province or princely mansion orders precede action, in food and travel every move must be reported; they sit straight, keeping their salary and following the law — none dares speak on loosening or tightening; the acting official holds the power, the registry clerk tugs their elbow; where petty gain is not granted, the blame for acting alone is already incurred.

sentences.zh: 處地雖重，行己莫由，威不在身，恩未接下，倉卒一朝，艱難總集，望其釋位扶危，不可得矣。

translations.literal: Though their station is weighty, they cannot act by themselves; authority is not in their hands, grace has not reached those below; in one hasty morning hardship gathers all at once — to expect them to yield their posts and steady the peril was impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Though their position was weighty, they could not act as they wished; awe was not in their persons, favor had not reached those below; in one sudden morning hardship gathered all together — to hope they would leave office and steady the crisis was impossible.
